एतान्पश्यन्ययौ वृक्षांस्ततो रैवतकं गिरिम् .. 12 ..
17.15.m: They fall within the range of vision only of those people whose deeds are virtuous. / Looking upon these trees, he then went to Mount Raivataka.

17.15.s:
yāvannirīkṣate tuṃgaṃ śikharaṃ tasya mūrddhani ..
āścaryaṃ dadṛśe vipro mahallokabhayaṃkaram .. 13 ..
17.15.d:
यावन्निरीक्षते तुंगं शिखरं तस्य मूर्द्धनि ..
आश्चर्यं ददृशे विप्रो महल्लोकभयंकरम् .. 13 ..
17.15.m: As he looked at its lofty peak, on its summit / the brahmin beheld a great wonder, terrifying to the world:

17.15.s:
dhūmajvalanamadhyasthānpuruṣānpaṃca paśyati ..
kṛṣṇāṃgānkhecarānraudrānkṛṣṇāguruvibhūṣitān .. 14 ..
17.15.d:
धूमज्वलनमध्यस्थान्पुरुषान्पंच पश्यति ..
कृष्णांगान्खेचरान्रौद्रान्कृष्णागुरुविभूषितान् .. 14 ..
17.15.m: he saw five men standing amid smoke and flame, / black-limbed, moving through the air, ferocious, adorned with black agallochum,

17.15.s:
sārameya samārūḍhānkarihastānsamekhalān ..
khaṅgakheṭakahastāṃśca ḍamaruḍḍāmarasvanān...35.
saghargharīkacaraṇanyāsanāditaparvatān ..
phetkārabhāsurākārānkāśakuñcitamūrddhajān .. 16 ..
naramāṃsavasāsārakavalavyagratālukān ..
janagaṃdhasamājñānabhavatīvravilocanān .. 17 ..
pañcāgnisādhanāvyāptadivyacakṣuḥ prabhāvataḥ ..
devānpaśyati viprendro jñātakāryaparaṃparaḥ .. 18 ..
ete kṣetrādhipāḥ pañca mahādevena nirmitāḥ ..
mahābalā raivatake nivasaṃti girau sadā .. .. 19 ..
svecchācārānnarānmarttyānvārayati nage tathā ..
hariṃ haraṃ nadīṃ devīṃ na paśyaṃti giriṃ yathā .. 7.2.15.20 ..
dṛṣṭvā jñātvā stutiṃ cakre dhyātvā devaṃ maheśvaram ..
jayaṃti duṣṭadaityeṃdrayuddhadhyānāṃkitaṃ vapuḥ ..
bibhrati bhrātaro ye te paṃceṃdrasamavikramāḥ .. 21 ..
17.15.d:
सारमेय समारूढान्करिहस्तान्समेखलान् ..
खङ्गखेटकहस्तांश्च डमरुड्डामरस्वनान्...35.

17.15.m:
mounted upon dogs, with hands like elephant trunks, wearing girdles, / with swords and shields in their hands, making sounds with ḍamarus and terrible noise,
making the mountain resound with the movement of feet wearing small ringing bells, / of radiant form accompanied by howls, with curly hair like kāśa grass,
their palates busy swallowing the marrow, fat, and flesh of humans, / whose eyes were fierce with the smell and recognition of people.
By the power of divine sight acquired through the practice of the five fires, / the foremost of brahmins, understanding the succession of duties, beheld the gods.
These are the five guardians of the sacred field, created by Mahādeva, / very powerful, who dwell constantly on Mount Raivataka.
They turn away mortal men on the mountain who act according to their own whim, / so that they do not see Hari, Hara, the river, the goddess, or the mountain.
Having seen and understood [them], he meditated on the lord Maheśvara and uttered a hymn of praise: / 'Victorious are those who bear bodies marked by meditating on battle with wicked lords of Daityas, / those five brothers who possess valour equal to Indra's!

17.15.m:
Born from the mouth of Rudra, capable, destroyers of Dakṣa's sacrifice, / celebrated by Brahmins terrified when their oblations swallowed by their own [flames] were ruined!
With limbs smeared with saffron, agallochum, and camphor, well-adorned, / divine beings whose limbs are intoxicated by the fragrance of wine, performing dances and songs!
Tired from wandering across the cosmic egg, their movements terrifying by their own scent, / swift as thought, moving at will—victorious are those kṣetrapālas!'
Pleased by these and other words, they stood before the twice-born and [one said]: / 'I am Ekapāda, the first, and the second is Giridāruṇa;
The third is Meghanāda, and Siṃhanāda is the fourth; / I, the fifth, am Kālamegha. Tell us, what shall we do for you?'
The twice-born said: / 'If you are pleased with me, if a boon is truly to be granted, / oh, consecrated by me, you must remain here until the dissolution of the universe!'
First, out of great joy, Ekapāda took his place on the slope of the mountain; / while he dwelt on the mountain in that dwelling-place, Giridāruṇa also,

17.15.m:
Having been installed and propitiated, that granter of boons took his stand himself. / Meghanāda went of his own accord to the summit of Mount Ujjayanta;
Likewise, Siṃhanāda entered the delightful Bhavānīśaṃkara; / he was assigned before Bhava in Vastrāpatha itself.
The mighty Kālamegha [took his stand] on the bank of the river Svarṇarekhā; / in ancient times, the sacred ford was established for the welfare of all the worlds.
Vāmana himself went and worshipped the kṣetrapālas. / Formerly, at the beginning of the yuga, O king of kings, all the gods assembled,
Arriving in the country of Surāṣṭra at the sacred mountain Raivataka, / for the protection of all the worlds and the destruction of the enemies of the gods.
Then a garland of victory was placed around the neck of Viṣṇu by the foremost gods; / the renowned, supreme name "Dāmodara" was bestowed upon Hari.
There, first, on a day beloved of Viṣṇu during the bright fortnight of Kārttika, / having fasted along with the gods, that sacred ford was created by Viṣṇu.

17.15.s:

17.15.m: Washing away all sins, destroying disease and poverty— / Dāmodara on Raivataka, bestowing supreme bliss.

उपवासेवन कृच्छ्रेण शाकाहारेण वा पुनः .. 41 ..
17.15.m: Or by [eating] a single meal, or at night, or [eating only] unasked-for food, / or by fasting, severe penance, or eating vegetables,

17.15.m: Viṣṇu should be served in Kārttika by people intent on offering lamps. / If the month is spent by men devoted to celibacy,

17.15.m: Then residence in the city of Viṣṇu is attained alongside Viṣṇu. / Five fasts should be observed when the Bhīṣmapañcaka arrives,

तदेतत्पंचकं प्रोक्तं सर्वपापहरं नृणाम्.. 44 ..
17.15.m: Beginning with the Ekādaśī up to the fifth day, the day of the full moon. / This is declared to be the Pañcaka that removes all sins of mortals.

17.15.s:

māsāṃte vividhaṃ deyaṃ gaustilāḥ kusumāni ca ..

सर्वदानेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्व तीर्थेषु यत्फलम्.. 47 ..
17.15.m: At the end of the month, various gifts should be given: a cow, sesame seeds, and flowers. / Whatever merit [is earned] in all gifts, whatever fruit [is gained] at all sacred fords,

17.15.s:

17.15.d:

तत्फलं जायते नॄणां दृष्टे दामोदरे नृप .. 48 ..
17.15.m: And whatever [fruit is attained] through sacrifices such as the horse sacrifice, or by offering funeral cakes at Gayā— / that fruit arises for mortals when Dāmodara is beheld, O king.

पूजयित्वा ततः पुष्पैः शतपत्रैः सुगं धिभिः .. 7.2.15.50 ..
17.15.m: Mixed with saffron, agallochum, sandalwood, and camphor water, / and then having worshipped him with fragrant, hundred-petalled flowers,

वस्त्रयज्ञोपवीतं च दत्त्वा धूपं प्रधूपयेत्..51..

17.15.m: Worship of the temple should be performed by dedicating a banner and other offerings, O king; / then a cow with its calf, which carries one across the ocean of worldly existence, should be given.

17.15.s:

17.15.m: Then, having circumambulated with sounds of singing and instrumental music, / and with recitations of the Vedas, Purāṇas, expositions, divine narratives, and the like,

17.15.d:
देवाग्रे जागरः कार्यो दीपो देयोंऽतिभूमिषु ..
सप्तधान्यमयाः सप्त पर्वता दीपसंयुताः .. 55 ..
17.15.m: A night vigil should be kept before the deity, and a lamp should be placed on high pedestals. / Seven mountains made of the seven grains, accompanied by lamps,

17.15.s:
phalatāṃbūlapakvānnapūritāḥ parikalpitāḥ ..
vidvadbhiḥ śrotriyaiḥ śrāṃtairbrāhmaṇairgṛhamedhibhiḥ .. 56 ..
17.15.d:
फलतांबूलपक्वान्नपूरिताः परिकल्पिताः ..
विद्वद्भिः श्रोत्रियैः श्रांतैर्ब्राह्मणैर्गृहमेधिभिः .. 56 ..
17.15.m: Filled with fruits, betel, and cooked delicacies, should be prepared / by learned men, Vedic scholars, disciplined brahmin householders,

17.15.s:
strībhiśca naraśārdūla śrotavyā vaiṣṇavī kathā ..
evaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ rāgakrodhavivarjitaiḥ .. 57 ..
17.15.d:
स्त्रीभिश्च नरशार्दूल श्रोतव्या वैष्णवी कथा ..
एवं जागरणं कार्यं रागक्रोधविवर्जितैः .. 57 ..
17.15.m: And by women, O tiger among men; a narrative of Viṣṇu should be listened to. / Thus a night vigil should be kept, free from passion and anger.

17.15.s:
kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ rātrāvudite sūryamaḍale ..
pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ tataḥ snātvā kṛtvā madhyāhnamācaret..58..
17.15.d:
कृत्वा जागरणं रात्रावुदिते सूर्यमडले ..
पूर्वां संध्यां ततः स्नात्वा कृत्वा मध्याह्नमाचरेत्..58..
17.15.m: Having observed the night vigil, when the disc of the sun has risen, / having bathed and performed the morning twilight devotion, one should attend to the midday rites.

17.15.s:
devānpitṝnmanuṣyāṃśca saṃtarpya vidhipūrvakam..
kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu dadyāddānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ.. 59..
17.15.d:
देवान्पितॄन्मनुष्यांश्च संतर्प्य विधिपूर्वकम्..
कृत्वा श्राद्धं पितॄणां तु दद्याद्दानं स्वशक्तितः.. 59..
17.15.m: Having duly made water offerings to the gods, ancestors, and human beings, / and having performed the ancestral rite for the ancestors, one should give gifts according to one's capacity.

17.15.s:
devaṃ dāmodaraṃ pūjya puṣpadhūpādinā punaḥ ..
narasiṃhaṃ suraṃ pūjya vainateyaṃ ca pūjayet .. 7.2.15.60 ..
17.15.d:
देवं दामोदरं पूज्य पुष्पधूपादिना पुनः ..
नरसिंहं सुरं पूज्य वैनतेयं च पूजयेत् .. 7.2.15.60 ..
17.15.m: Having worshipped the god Dāmodara again with flowers, incense, and the like, / and having worshipped the god Narasiṃha, one should also worship Garuḍa.

17.15.s:
kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ rātrāvutthāpya madhusūdanam ..
dvādaśībhuktimāsādya kāryaṃ pāraṇakaṃ naraiḥ .. 61 ..
17.15.d:
कृत्वा जागरणं रात्रावुत्थाप्य मधुसूदनम् ..
द्वादशीभुक्तिमासाद्य कार्यं पारणकं नरैः .. 61 ..
17.15.m: Having kept the night vigil, having awakened Madhusūdana, / and having obtained the meal of Dvādaśī, the breaking of the fast should be performed by people.

17.15.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā ca sahitaḥ putrabāṃdhavaiḥ ..
vikalāṃdhakṛpaṇānāṃ deyamannaṃ svaśaktitaḥ .. 62 ..
17.15.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयित्वा च सहितः पुत्रबांधवैः ..
विकलांधकृपणानां देयमन्नं स्वशक्तितः .. 62 ..
17.15.m: Having fed brahmins, together with sons and kinsmen, / food should be given according to one's ability to the disabled, the blind, and the destitute.

17.15.s:
dāmodare raivatake svarṇarekhānadījale ..
evaṃ yaḥ kurute yātrāṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 63 ..
17.15.d:
दामोदरे रैवतके स्वर्णरेखानदीजले ..
एवं यः कुरुते यात्रां तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 63 ..
17.15.m: Whoever thus undertakes a pilgrimage to Dāmodara on Raivataka, in the waters of the river Svarṇarekhā, / hear the meritorious fruit of that person:

17.15.s:
brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca grāmasīmāvilopakaḥ ..
rājadrohī gurudrohī mithyāvratadharaśca yaḥ .. 64 ..
17.15.d:
ब्रह्मघ्नश्च सुरापश्च ग्रामसीमाविलोपकः ..
राजद्रोही गुरुद्रोही मिथ्याव्रतधरश्च यः .. 64 ..
17.15.m: A slayer of a brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a destroyer of village boundaries, / one who betrays the king, one who betrays the teacher, and one who keeps false vows,

17.15.s:
kūṭasākṣyaprado yaśca yaśca nyāsāpahārakaḥ ..
bālastrīghātako vipraḥ saṃdhyāsnānavivarjitaḥ .. 65 ..
17.15.d:
कूटसाक्ष्यप्रदो यश्च यश्च न्यासापहारकः ..
बालस्त्रीघातको विप्रः संध्यास्नानविवर्जितः .. 65 ..
17.15.m: he who gives false testimony, and he who appropriates a deposit, / a brahmin who kills a child or a woman, one devoid of twilight prayers and ritual ablution,

17.15.s:
devabrahma svaharttā ca vedavikrayakārakaḥ ..
kanyāvikrayakarttā ca devabrāhmaṇaniṃdakaḥ ..66..
17.15.d:
देवब्रह्म स्वहर्त्ता च वेदविक्रयकारकः ..
कन्याविक्रयकर्त्ता च देवब्राह्मणनिंदकः ..66..
17.15.m: he who steals the property of deities or brahmins, he who sells the Vedas, / he who sells his daughter, and he who reviles deities and brahmins,

17.15.s:
viśvāsaghātako vipraḥ śūdrānnādo'tha lubdhakaḥ ..
nāyakaḥ paradārāṇāṃ svayaṃdattāpahārakaḥ .. 67 ..
17.15.d:
विश्वासघातको विप्रः शूद्रान्नादोऽथ लुब्धकः ..
नायकः परदाराणां स्वयंदत्तापहारकः .. 67 ..
17.15.m: a brahmin who betrays trust, one who eats the food of a Śūdra, a hunter, / a seducer of others' wives, one who takes back what he himself gave,

17.15.s:
parvamaithunasevī ca tathā vai setubhedakaḥ ..
pariṇītāmṛtusnātāṃ svayaṃ yo nābhigacchati .. 68 ..
17.15.d:
पर्वमैथुनसेवी च तथा वै सेतुभेदकः ..
परिणीतामृतुस्नातां स्वयं यो नाभिगच्छति .. 68 ..
17.15.m: one who indulges in sexual intercourse on sacred days, likewise a breaker of dams, / he who does not himself approach his wedded wife who has bathed after her courses,

17.15.s:
brāhmaṇī vidhavā bālā na bhavecchrutadhāriṇī ..
mahāpātakinaścaite tathānye bahavo nṛpa .. 69 ..
17.15.d:
ब्राह्मणी विधवा बाला न भवेच्छ्रुतधारिणी ..
महापातकिनश्चैते तथान्ये बहवो नृप .. 69 ..
17.15.m: a young brahmin widow who does not uphold the sacred tradition— / these and many others are great sinners, O king.

17.15.s:
svarṇarekhājale snātvā dṛṣṭvā dāmodaraṃ harim ..
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ .. 7.2.15.70 ..
17.15.d:
स्वर्णरेखाजले स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा दामोदरं हरिम् ..
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः .. 7.2.15.70 ..
17.15.m: Having bathed in the waters of the Svarṇarekhā, having beheld Hari as Dāmodara, / and having kept a night-vigil, one is liberated from all sins.

17.15.s:
na tu ye pāpakarmāṇaḥ samāyātāḥ prajāgare ..
saṃsārasāgare tīrthe gacchaṃti na hareḥ puram .. 71 ..
17.15.d:
न तु ये पापकर्माणः समायाताः प्रजागरे ..
संसारसागरे तीर्थे गच्छंति न हरेः पुरम् .. 71 ..
17.15.m: But those evil-doers who do not assemble for the vigil / at the sacred ford on the ocean of worldly existence do not go to the city of Hari.

17.15.s:
yathā yathā yāti naraḥ prajāgare tathātathā viṣṇupure viciṃtyate ..
vāsaḥ surairvaiṣṇavalokahetave mṛdaṃgagītadhvaninādite gṛhe .. 72 ..
17.15.d:
यथा यथा याति नरः प्रजागरे तथातथा विष्णुपुरे विचिंत्यते ..
वासः सुरैर्वैष्णवलोकहेतवे मृदंगगीतध्वनिनादिते गृहे .. 72 ..
17.15.m: As a man keeps the vigil, so do the gods contemplate his residence in the city of Viṣṇu / for the sake of the Vaiṣṇava realm, in an abode resounding with the sound of mṛdaṅgas and songs.

17.15.s:
gadāsi śaṃkhāridharāścaturbhujā daiteyadarpāpaharūpadhāriṇaḥ ..
pragīyamānāḥ surasuṃdarībhiste yāṃti khaṃ khecaragātrasaṃgāḥ .. 73 ..
17.15.d:
गदासि शंखारिधराश्चतुर्भुजा दैतेयदर्पापहरूपधारिणः ..
प्रगीयमानाः सुरसुंदरीभिस्ते यांति खं खेचरगात्रसंगाः .. 73 ..
17.15.m: Bearing mace, sword, conch, and discus, four-armed, assuming the form that removes the pride of the Daityas, / praised in song by divine beauties, touching the bodies of celestial wanderers, they go to the sky.

17.15.s:
vārāhakalpe prathamaṃ yugādau dāmodaro raivatake prasiddhaḥ ..
saiṣā nadī yā saritāṃ variṣṭhā so'yaṃ hariryo bhuvanasya kartā .. 74 ..
17.15.d:
वाराहकल्पे प्रथमं युगादौ दामोदरो रैवतके प्रसिद्धः ..
सैषा नदी या सरितां वरिष्ठा सोऽयं हरिर्यो भुवनस्य कर्ता .. 74 ..
17.15.m: In the Vārāha Kalpa, at the beginning of the yuga, Dāmodara first became renowned on Raivataka; / this is that river which is the best among rivers; this is that Hari who is the maker of the world.

17.15.s:
idaṃ purāṇaṃ paṭhate śṛṇoti naro vimānairmadhusūda nālaye ..
devāṃganādattabhujaścaturbhujaḥ sa nīyate devagaṇairabhiṣṭutaḥ .. 75 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsa khaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye sārasvataproktatīrthayātrāvidhāne śrīdāmodaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma paṃcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ ..15..
17.15.d:
इदं पुराणं पठते शृणोति नरो विमानैर्मधुसूद नालये ..
देवांगनादत्तभुजश्चतुर्भुजः स नीयते देवगणैरभिष्टुतः .. 75 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभास खण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सारस्वतप्रोक्ततीर्थयात्राविधाने श्रीदामोदरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम पंचदशोऽध्यायः ..15..
17.15.m:
A man who recites or listens to this Purāṇa is led in aerial chariots to the abode of Madhusūdana, / supported by the arms of divine maidens, four-armed, praised by hosts of gods.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Śrī Dāmodara' in the Rules for Pilgrimage to Sacred Fords Proclaimed by Sārasvata, in the Vastrāpathakṣetra-māhātmya, in the second [sub-section of the] Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of Śrī Skanda, in the Saṃhitā of eighty-one thousand [verses].

17.16.s:
.. rājovāca ..
athāsau vāmano vipraḥ praviṣṭo gahane vane ..
ekākī kiṃ cakārātha kautukaṃ tadvadasva me .. 1 ..
17.16.d:
.. राजोवाच ..
अथासौ वामनो विप्रः प्रविष्टो गहने वने ..
एकाकी किं चकाराथ कौतुकं तद्वदस्व मे .. 1 ..
17.16.m: The king said: / Now, when that brahmin Vāmana entered the deep forest, / what wonder did he perform there alone? Tell me that.

17.16.s:
.. sārasvata uvāca .. ..
athāsau vāmano vipro gatvā raivatake girau ..
svarṇarekhānadītoye snātvātha vidhipūrvakam .. 2 ..
17.16.d:
.. सारस्वत उवाच .. ..
अथासौ वामनो विप्रो गत्वा रैवतके गिरौ ..
स्वर्णरेखानदीतोये स्नात्वाथ विधिपूर्वकम् .. 2 ..
17.16.m: Sārasvata said: / Then that brahmin Vāmana, having gone to Mount Raivataka, / and having bathed according to rule in the waters of the river Svarṇarekhā,

17.16.s:
sugaṃdhapuṣpadhūpādyairdevaṃ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ ..
tasthau tadagrato rājannekākī nirjane vane ..3 ..
17.16.d:
सुगंधपुष्पधूपाद्यैर्देवं संपूज्य भक्तितः ..
तस्थौ तदग्रतो राजन्नेकाकी निर्जने वने ..3 ..
17.16.m: having worshipped the god with devotion using fragrant flowers, incense, and the like, / stood before him alone in the desolate forest, O king,

17.16.s:
sarvasattvasamāyukte sarīsṛpasamākule..
anekasvarasaṃghuṣṭe mayūradhvaninādite .. 4 ..
17.16.d:
सर्वसत्त्वसमायुक्ते सरीसृपसमाकुले..
अनेकस्वरसंघुष्टे मयूरध्वनिनादिते .. 4 ..
17.16.m: a forest filled with all kinds of creatures, swarming with reptiles, / resounding with many calls, echoing with the cries of peacocks,

17.16.s:
kokilārāvaramye ca vanakukkuṭaghoṣite ..
khadyotadyotite tasminvalīmukhavidhūnite ..5..
17.16.d:
कोकिलारावरम्ये च वनकुक्कुटघोषिते ..
खद्योतद्योतिते तस्मिन्वलीमुखविधूनिते ..5..
17.16.m: charming with the cries of cuckoos, noisy with wild cocks, / illuminated by fireflies, shaken by monkeys,

17.16.s:
kvacidvaṃśāgninā śāṃte kvacitpuṣpitapādape ..
gaganāsaktaviṭape sūryatāpavivarjite ..6..
17.16.d:
क्वचिद्वंशाग्निना शांते क्वचित्पुष्पितपादपे ..
गगनासक्तविटपे सूर्यतापविवर्जिते ..6..
17.16.m: calmed in places by bamboo-fires, with blossoming trees in places, / its branches touching the sky, free from the heat of the sun,

17.16.s:
lubdhakāghāta saṃtrastabhrāṃtasūkaraśaṃbare ..
saṃhṛṣṭakṣatriyavātasthānadānavicakṣaṇe .. 7..
17.16.d:
लुब्धकाघात संत्रस्तभ्रांतसूकरशंबरे ..
संहृष्टक्षत्रियवातस्थानदानविचक्षणे .. 7..
17.16.m: with wild boars and śambara deer wandering in terror from the strikes of hunters, / skillful in providing places of safety for hosts of delighted Kṣatriyas.

17.16.s:
anekāścaryasaṃpannaṃ sasmāra manasā harim ..
taṃ bhītamiva vijñāya narasiṃhaḥ samāyayau .. 8 ..
17.16.d:
अनेकाश्चर्यसंपन्नं सस्मार मनसा हरिम् ..
तं भीतमिव विज्ञाय नरसिंहः समाययौ .. 8 ..
17.16.m: Endowed with many wonders, he remembered Hari with his mind. / Knowing him to be frightened, as it were, Narasiṃha arrived.

17.16.s:
rakṣārthaṃ tasya viprasya babhāṣe purataḥ sthitaḥ ..
na bhetavyaṃ tvayā vipra vada te kiṃ karomyaham .. 9 ..
17.16.d:
रक्षार्थं तस्य विप्रस्य बभाषे पुरतः स्थितः ..
न भेतव्यं त्वया विप्र वद ते किं करोम्यहम् .. 9 ..
17.16.m: For the protection of that brahmin, standing before him, he spoke: / 'You must not fear, O brahmin; tell me, what shall I do for you?'

17.16.s:
.. vipra uvāca .. ..
yadi tuṣṭo varo deyo narasiṃha tvayā mama ..
sadātra rakṣā karttavyā sarveṣāṃ tīrthavāsinām ..7.2.16.10 ..
17.16.d:
.. विप्र उवाच .. ..
यदि तुष्टो वरो देयो नरसिंह त्वया मम ..
सदात्र रक्षा कर्त्तव्या सर्वेषां तीर्थवासिनाम् ..7.2.16.10 ..
17.16.m: The brahmin said: / 'If you are pleased and a boon is to be given to me by you, O Narasiṃha, / protection must always be granted here to all dwellers at the sacred ford.

17.16.s:
devasyāgre sadā stheyaṃ yāvadiṃdrāścaturddaśa ..
evamastviti taṃ procya tathā cakre haristadā .. 11 ..
17.16.d:
देवस्याग्रे सदा स्थेयं यावदिंद्राश्चतुर्द्दश ..
एवमस्त्विति तं प्रोच्य तथा चक्रे हरिस्तदा .. 11 ..
17.16.m: You must always remain before the deity as long as the fourteen Indras [endure].' / Saying 'Let it be so' to him, Hari then acted accordingly.

17.16.s:
ato dāmodarasyāgre narasiṃhaḥ sa pūjyate ..
vanaṃ saumyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena tīrtharakṣāṃ karoti saḥ .. 12 ..
17.16.d:
अतो दामोदरस्याग्रे नरसिंहः स पूज्यते ..
वनं सौम्यं कृतं तेन तीर्थरक्षां करोति सः .. 12 ..
17.16.m: Therefore, Narasiṃha is worshipped before Dāmodara; / the forest was made tranquil by him, and he protects the sacred ford.

17.16.s:
bhūtapretādisaṃvāso vane tasminna jāyate ..
narasiṃhaprabhāvena naṣṭaṃ siṃhādijaṃ bhayam .. 13..
17.16.d:
भूतप्रेतादिसंवासो वने तस्मिन्न जायते ..
नरसिंहप्रभावेन नष्टं सिंहादिजं भयम् .. 13..
17.16.m: No dwelling of bhūtas, pretas, and the like occurs in that forest; / by the power of Narasiṃha, fear arising from lions and other beasts was destroyed.

17.16.s:
kārttike vāsare viṣṇordvādaśyāṃ pāraṇe kṛte ..
dāmodaraṃ namaskṛtya bhavaṃ draṣṭuṃ tato yayau .. 14 ..
17.16.d:
कार्त्तिके वासरे विष्णोर्द्वादश्यां पारणे कृते ..
दामोदरं नमस्कृत्य भवं द्रष्टुं ततो ययौ .. 14 ..
17.16.m: In the month of Kārttika, on the day of Viṣṇu, on the twelfth lunar day, after breaking his fast, / having bowed to Dāmodara, he then went to behold Bhava.

17.16.s:
caturdaśyāṃ kṛtasnāno bhavaṃ saṃpūjya bhāvataḥ ..
bhavabhāvabhavaṃ pāpaṃ bhasmībhūtaṃ bhavārcanāt .. 15..
17.16.d:
चतुर्दश्यां कृतस्नानो भवं संपूज्य भावतः ..
भवभावभवं पापं भस्मीभूतं भवार्चनात् .. 15..
17.16.m: Having bathed on the fourteenth lunar day and worshipped Bhava with devotion, / the sin arising from worldly existence was reduced to ashes from the worship of Bhava.

17.16.s:
sa kṣīṇapāpanicayo jāto devasya darśanāt ..
bhavasyāgre sthitaṃ śāṃtaṃ tathā vastrāpathasya ca .. 16..
17.16.d:
स क्षीणपापनिचयो जातो देवस्य दर्शनात् ..
भवस्याग्रे स्थितं शांतं तथा वस्त्रापथस्य च .. 16..
17.16.m: His heap of sins diminished from beholding the deity; / [he saw] that tranquil one standing before Bhava and likewise Vastrāpatha.

17.16.s:
taṃ kālameghaṃ samabhyarcya tato vastrāpathaṃ yayau ..
devaṃ saṃpūjya maṃtraiḥ sa vedoktairvidhipūrvakam .. 17 ..
17.16.d:
तं कालमेघं समभ्यर्च्य ततो वस्त्रापथं ययौ ..
देवं संपूज्य मंत्रैः स वेदोक्तैर्विधिपूर्वकम् .. 17 ..
17.16.m: Having worshipped that Kālamegha, he then went to Vastrāpatha; / having worshipped the deity with mantras declared in the Vedas, according to rule,

17.16.s:
dhūpadīpādinaivedyaiḥ sarvaṃ cakre sa vāmanaḥ ..
pradakṣiṇāśataṃ kṛtvā bhavasyāgre vyavasthitaḥ .. 18 ..
17.16.d:
धूपदीपादिनैवेद्यैः सर्वं चक्रे स वामनः ..
प्रदक्षिणाशतं कृत्वा भवस्याग्रे व्यवस्थितः .. 18 ..
17.16.m: with incense, lamps, food offerings, and the like, Vāmana performed everything. / Having performed a hundred circumambulations, he stood before Bhava.

17.16.s:
yāvannirīkṣate sarvaṃ tāvatpaśyati parvatam ..
ujjayaṃtaṃ girivaraṃ mainākasya sahodaram .. 19 ..
17.16.d:
यावन्निरीक्षते सर्वं तावत्पश्यति पर्वतम् ..
उज्जयंतं गिरिवरं मैनाकस्य सहोदरम् .. 19 ..
17.16.m: As he looks upon everything, he beholds the mountain, / Ujjayanta, the best of mountains, the brother of Maināka,

17.16.s:
surāṣṭradeśe vikhyātaṃ yugādau prathamaṃ sthitam ..
bhūdharaṃ bhūdharairyuktaṃ śilāpādapamaṃḍitam .. 7.2.16.20 ..
17.16.d:
सुराष्ट्रदेशे विख्यातं युगादौ प्रथमं स्थितम् ..
भूधरं भूधरैर्युक्तं शिलापादपमंडितम् .. 7.2.16.20 ..
17.16.m: renowned in the land of Surāṣṭra, situated first at the beginning of the yuga, / a mountain joined with hills, adorned with rocks and trees.

17.16.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā ciṃtayāmāsa sūkṣmāndharmānsa vāmanaḥ ..
alpāyāsānsubahulānputralakṣmīpradāyakān .. 21 ..
17.16.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा चिंतयामास सूक्ष्मान्धर्मान्स वामनः ..
अल्पायासान्सुबहुलान्पुत्रलक्ष्मीप्रदायकान् .. 21 ..
17.16.m: Having seen it, that Vāmana reflected upon the subtle dharmas, / requiring little effort, bringing abundant results, bestowing sons and prosperity:

17.16.s:
avaśyaṃ kriya māṇeṣu svadharma upajāyate ..
dṛṣṭvā nadīṃ sāgaragāṃ snātvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 22 ..
17.16.d:
अवश्यं क्रिय माणेषु स्वधर्म उपजायते ..
दृष्ट्वा नदीं सागरगां स्नात्वा पापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 22 ..
17.16.m: 'When [these duties] are performed, one's own dharma arises inevitably: / having seen a river flowing to the ocean and having bathed, one is freed from sins;

17.16.s:
gāṃ spṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇaṃ natvā saṃpūjya gurudevatāḥ ..
tapasvinaṃ yatiṃ śāṃtaṃ śrotriyaṃ brahmacāriṇam .. 23 ..
17.16.d:
गां स्पृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मणं नत्वा संपूज्य गुरुदेवताः ..
तपस्विनं यतिं शांतं श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मचारिणम् .. 23 ..
17.16.m: having touched a cow, having bowed to a brahmin, having worshipped the guru and deities, / an ascetic, a restrained renouncer, a Veda-knowing scholar, a celibate student;

17.16.s:
pitaraṃ mātaraṃ bhaginīṃ tatpatiṃ duhitāṃ patim ..
bhāgineyamatha dauhitraṃ mitrasaṃbadhibāṃdhavān ..
saṃbhojya pātakaiḥ sarvairmucyaṃte gṛhamedhinaḥ .. 24 ..
17.16.d:
पितरं मातरं भगिनीं तत्पतिं दुहितां पतिम् ..
भागिनेयमथ दौहित्रं मित्रसंबधिबांधवान् ..
संभोज्य पातकैः सर्वैर्मुच्यंते गृहमेधिनः .. 24 ..
17.16.m: having fed father, mother, sister, her husband, daughter, husband, / nephew, grandson, friends, relatives, and kin, householders are freed from all sins.

17.16.s:
rājā gajāśvanakulaṃ satīvṛṣamahīdharāḥ ..
ādarśakṣīravṛkṣāśca satatānnapradāstu te .. 25 ..
17.16.d:
राजा गजाश्वनकुलं सतीवृषमहीधराः ..
आदर्शक्षीरवृक्षाश्च सततान्नप्रदास्तु ते .. 25 ..
17.16.m: A king, an elephant, a horse, a mongoose, a chaste woman, a bull, mountains, / a mirror, trees with milky sap, and those who continually provide food—

17.16.s:
dṛṣṭamātrāḥ punantyete ye nityaṃ satyavādinaḥ ..
vedadharmakathāṃ śrutvā bhuktimuktipradā narān ..26..
17.16.d:
दृष्टमात्राः पुनन्त्येते ये नित्यं सत्यवादिनः ..
वेदधर्मकथां श्रुत्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदा नरान् ..26..
17.16.m: these purify as soon as they are seen, [as do] those who always speak the truth; / having heard a discourse on the dharma of the Vedas, they bestow enjoyment and liberation upon men.

17.16.s:
smṛtvā hariharau gaṃgāṃ kṛtvā tīreṇa mārjanam ..
gatvā jāgaraṇe viṣṇordattvā dānaṃ ca śaktitaḥ .. 27..
17.16.d:
स्मृत्वा हरिहरौ गंगां कृत्वा तीरेण मार्जनम् ..
गत्वा जागरणे विष्णोर्दत्त्वा दानं च शक्तितः .. 27..
17.16.m: Remembering Hari and Hara and the Gaṅgā, performing cleansing by its bank, / going to the vigil of Viṣṇu and giving a gift according to one's capacity,

17.16.s:
tāṃbūlaṃ kusumaṃ dīpaṃ naivedyaṃ tulasīdalam ..
gītaṃ nṛtyaṃ ca vādyaṃ ca vidhāya suramaṃdire .. 28 ..
17.16.d:
तांबूलं कुसुमं दीपं नैवेद्यं तुलसीदलम् ..
गीतं नृत्यं च वाद्यं च विधाय सुरमंदिरे .. 28 ..
17.16.m: offering betel, flowers, a lamp, food offerings, and tulasī leaves, / and performing singing, dancing, and instrumental music in the temple of the god—

17.16.s:
ete sūkṣmāḥ smṛtā dharmāḥ kriyamāṇā mahodayāḥ ..
ato girīndraṃ paśyāmi sarvadevālayaṃ śubham ..29 ..
17.16.d:
एते सूक्ष्माः स्मृता धर्माः क्रियमाणा महोदयाः ..
अतो गिरीन्द्रं पश्यामि सर्वदेवालयं शुभम् ..29 ..
17.16.m: these are remembered as the subtle dharmas which, when performed, bring great prosperity. / Therefore, I shall behold the lord of mountains, the auspicious abode of all the gods.'

17.16.s: teṣāṃ karatale svargaḥ śikharaṃ yāṃti ye narāḥ .. 7.2.16.30..
17.16.m: Heaven is in the palm of their hand—those men who ascend the peak. (30)

17.16.s:
iti jñātvā samā rūḍho vāmano girimūrddhani ..
airāvatapadākrāṃtyā yatra toyaṃ viniḥsṛtam ..31..
17.16.d:
इति ज्ञात्वा समा रूढो वामनो गिरिमूर्द्धनि ..
ऐरावतपदाक्रांत्या यत्र तोयं विनिःसृतम् ..31..
17.16.m: Knowing this, Vāmana climbed to the mountain summit, / where water had gushed forth from the impact of Airāvata's foot. (31)

17.16.s:
tataḥ śikharamārūḍhāṃ bhavānīṃ skandamātaram ..
draṣṭuṃ sa vāmano yāti śikhare gaganāśrite .. 32 ..
17.16.d:
ततः शिखरमारूढां भवानीं स्कन्दमातरम् ..
द्रष्टुं स वामनो याति शिखरे गगनाश्रिते .. 32 ..
17.16.m: Then, to see Bhavānī, mother of Skanda, seated on the peak, / that Vāmana went up to the sky-reaching summit. (32)

17.16.s:
yathāyathā girivare samārohaṃti mānavāḥ ..
tathātathā vimucyaṃte pātakaiḥ sarvadehinaḥ .. 33 ..
17.16.d:
यथायथा गिरिवरे समारोहंति मानवाः ..
तथातथा विमुच्यंते पातकैः सर्वदेहिनः .. 33 ..
17.16.m: The higher men ascend upon the excellent mountain, / the more all embodied beings are freed from their sins. (33)

17.16.s:
iti kṛtvā matiṃ vipro jagāma girimūrddhani ..
bhavabhakto bhavānīṃ sa dadarśa skandamātaram ..34..
17.16.d:
इति कृत्वा मतिं विप्रो जगाम गिरिमूर्द्धनि ..
भवभक्तो भवानीं स ददर्श स्कन्दमातरम् ..34..
17.16.m: Resolving thus in his mind, the brahmin went to the mountain summit. / Devoted to Bhava, he beheld Bhavānī, the mother of Skanda. (34)

17.16.s:
aṃbeti bhāṣate skaṃdastato'nye sarvadevatāḥ ..
pṛthivyāṃ mānavāḥ sarve pātāle sarvapannagāḥ .. 35 ..
17.16.d:
अंबेति भाषते स्कंदस्ततोऽन्ये सर्वदेवताः ..
पृथिव्यां मानवाः सर्वे पाताले सर्वपन्नगाः .. 35 ..
17.16.m: "Mother!" says Skanda, and after him all the other gods, / all mortals on earth, and all serpents in Pātāla. (35)

17.16.s:
ato hyaṃbeti vikhyātā pūjyate girimūrddhani ..
saṃpūjya vividhairmukhyaiḥ phalairnānāvidhairdvijaḥ .. 36 ..
17.16.d:
अतो ह्यंबेति विख्याता पूज्यते गिरिमूर्द्धनि ..
संपूज्य विविधैर्मुख्यैः फलैर्नानाविधैर्द्विजः .. 36 ..
17.16.m: Therefore indeed she is celebrated as 'Ambā' and worshipped on the mountain summit. / Having worshipped her with various choice fruits of diverse kinds, the twice-born (36)

17.16.s:
gaganāsaktaśikhare saṃsthitaḥ kautukānvitaḥ ..
ekākī śikhare tasminnūrddhvabāhurvyavasthitaḥ ..37..
17.16.d:
गगनासक्तशिखरे संस्थितः कौतुकान्वितः ..
एकाकी शिखरे तस्मिन्नूर्द्ध्वबाहुर्व्यवस्थितः ..37..
17.16.m: stood upon the sky-touching peak filled with wonder. / Alone on that peak, he stood with his arms raised up, (37)

17.16.s:
nirīkṣya medinīṃ sarvāṃ saparvatasasāgarām..
ādyaṃ sanātanaṃ devaṃ bhāskaraṃ triguṇātmakam ..38..
17.16.d:
निरीक्ष्य मेदिनीं सर्वां सपर्वतससागराम्..
आद्यं सनातनं देवं भास्करं त्रिगुणात्मकम् ..38..
17.16.m: beholding the whole earth together with mountains and oceans, / [and gazing upon] the primordial, eternal god Bhāskara, composed of the three guṇas, (38)

17.16.s:
sarvatejomayaṃ sarvadevaṃ devairnamaskṛtam ..
bhramamāṇaṃ nirādhāraṃ kālamānaprayojakam ..39..
17.16.d:
सर्वतेजोमयं सर्वदेवं देवैर्नमस्कृतम् ..
भ्रममाणं निराधारं कालमानप्रयोजकम् ..39..
17.16.m: consisting of all radiance, the god of all, bowed to by the gods, / wandering without support, the instigator of the measurement of time. (39)

17.16.s:
yāvatpaśyati taṃ viprastāvatpaśyati śaṃkaram ..
digaṃbaraṃ bhavaṃ devaṃ samaṃtādaśmaguṃṭhitam .. 7.2.16.40 ..
17.16.d:
यावत्पश्यति तं विप्रस्तावत्पश्यति शंकरम् ..
दिगंबरं भवं देवं समंतादश्मगुंठितम् .. 7.2.16.40 ..
17.16.m: While the brahmin looked at him, just then he beheld Śaṃkara, / the sky-clad god Bhava, concealed on every side by stones, (40)

17.16.s:
buddharūpākṛtiṃ devaṃ sarvajñaṃ guṇabhūṣitam ..
kṛśāṃgaṃ jaṭilaṃ saumyaṃ vyomamārge svayaṃ sthitam .. 41 .. ..
17.16.d:
बुद्धरूपाकृतिं देवं सर्वज्ञं गुणभूषितम् ..
कृशांगं जटिलं सौम्यं व्योममार्गे स्वयं स्थितम् .. 41 .. ..
17.16.m: the god endowed with the appearance of the Buddha, omniscient, adorned with virtues, / lean-limbed, matted-haired, gentle, standing himself in the sky. (41)

17.16.s:
.. śrīśiva uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu vāmana tuṣṭo'haṃ dāsye te vividhānvarān ..
trailokyavyāpinī vṛddhirbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ .. 42 ..
17.16.d:
.. श्रीशिव उवाच .. ..
शृणु वामन तुष्टोऽहं दास्ये ते विविधान्वरान् ..
त्रैलोक्यव्यापिनी वृद्धिर्भविष्यति न संशयः .. 42 ..
17.16.m: Śrī Śiva said: / Listen, Vāmana! I am pleased; I will grant you various boons. / You shall have prosperity pervading the three worlds, there is no doubt. (42)

17.16.s:
pratibhāsyaṃti te vedā gītanṛtyādikaṃ ca yat ..
asādhyasādhanī śakti bhaviṣyati tava sthirā ..
paraṃ vastrāpathe gatvā kuru tīrthāvalokanam .. 43 ..
17.16.d:
प्रतिभास्यंति ते वेदा गीतनृत्यादिकं च यत् ..
असाध्यसाधनी शक्ति भविष्यति तव स्थिरा ..
परं वस्त्रापथे गत्वा कुरु तीर्थावलोकनम् .. 43 ..
17.16.m: The Vedas shall be revealed to you, as well as song, dance, and the like. / You will have steadfast power that accomplishes what is impossible. / Moreover, go to Vastrāpatha and behold the sacred fords. (43)

17.16.s:
.. vāmana uvāca .. ..
vastrāpathe mahādeva yāni tīrthāni tāni me ..
vada deva viśeṣeṇa yadyasti karuṇā mayi ..44..
17.16.d:
.. वामन उवाच .. ..
वस्त्रापथे महादेव यानि तीर्थानि तानि मे ..
वद देव विशेषेण यद्यस्ति करुणा मयि ..44..
17.16.m: Vāmana said: / Whatever sacred fords there are in Vastrāpatha, O Mahādeva, / declare them to me in detail, O God, if you have compassion for me. (44)

17.16.s:
.. rudra uvāca .. ..
vastrāpathasya vāyavye koṇe divyaṃ sarovaram ..
tasya paścimadigbhāge jālirgahanapallavā .. 45 ..
17.16.d:
.. रुद्र उवाच .. ..
वस्त्रापथस्य वायव्ये कोणे दिव्यं सरोवरम् ..
तस्य पश्चिमदिग्भागे जालिर्गहनपल्लवा .. 45 ..
17.16.m: Rudra said: / In the north-western corner of Vastrāpatha is a divine lake. / In its western quarter is a thicket dense with leaves, (45)

17.16.s:
bilvavṛkṣamayī madhye liṃgaṃ tatrāsti mṛnmayam ..
yatrāsau lubdhakaḥ siddho gato mama pure purā .. 46 ..
17.16.d:
बिल्ववृक्षमयी मध्ये लिंगं तत्रास्ति मृन्मयम् ..
यत्रासौ लुब्धकः सिद्धो गतो मम पुरे पुरा .. 46 ..
17.16.m: consisting of bilva trees; within it is an earthen liṅga / where that hunter of old attained perfection and went to my abode. (46)

17.16.s:
tasya darśanamātreṇa brahmahatyā vinaśyati ..
iṃdro vai vṛtrahā yasminvimukto brahmahatyayā .. 47 ..
17.16.d:
तस्य दर्शनमात्रेण ब्रह्महत्या विनश्यति ..
इंद्रो वै वृत्रहा यस्मिन्विमुक्तो ब्रह्महत्यया .. 47 ..
17.16.m: By merely viewing it, the sin of killing a brahmin is destroyed, / [the liṅga] where Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, was freed from the sin of killing a brahmin. (47)

17.16.s:
tasmādruttaradigbhāge dhanadena pratiṣṭhitam ..
liṃgaṃ trailokyavikhyātaṃ tatra devī triśūlinī .. 48 ..
17.16.d:
तस्माद्रुत्तरदिग्भागे धनदेन प्रतिष्ठितम् ..
लिंगं त्रैलोक्यविख्यातं तत्र देवी त्रिशूलिनी .. 48 ..
17.16.m: In the northern quarter from it is the liṅga established by Kubera, / famous in the three worlds; and there is the trident-bearing Goddess, (48)

17.16.s:
yasyā darśanamātreṇa putro'sya nalakūbara..
pāśānuṣaktahasto'bhūddevaṃ cakre triśūlinam .. 49 ..
17.16.d:
यस्या दर्शनमात्रेण पुत्रोऽस्य नलकूबर..
पाशानुषक्तहस्तोऽभूद्देवं चक्रे त्रिशूलिनम् .. 49 ..
17.16.m: by merely beholding whom his son Nalakūbara / came to have a noose fastened around his hand, and made the god trident-bearing. (49)

17.16.s:
bhavasya nairṛte koṇe gaṇo heraṃbasaṃjñitaḥ ..
yamena kurvatā liṃgaṃ prathamaṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ .. 7.2.16.50 ..
17.16.d:
भवस्य नैरृते कोणे गणो हेरंबसंज्ञितः ..
यमेन कुर्वता लिंगं प्रथमं च प्रतिष्ठितः .. 7.2.16.50 ..
17.16.m: In the south-western corner of Bhava, the attendant named Heramba / was first established by Yama while making the liṅga. (50)

17.16.s:
vicitraṃ tasya māhātmyaṃ citragupto'ti vismitaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā samāgato draṣṭuṃ devaṃ taṃ mṛnmayaṃ purā .. 51 ..
17.16.d:
विचित्रं तस्य माहात्म्यं चित्रगुप्तोऽति विस्मितः ..
दृष्ट्वा समागतो द्रष्टुं देवं तं मृन्मयं पुरा .. 51 ..
17.16.m: Wondrous is its māhātmya; Chitragupta was utterly amazed / upon seeing it, having come of old to see that earthen god. (51)

17.16.s:
tenāpi nirmitaṃ liṃgaṃ tasminkṣetre dvijottama ..
citragupteśvaraṃnāma vikhyātaṃ bhuvana traye .. 52 ..
17.16.d:
तेनापि निर्मितं लिंगं तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे द्विजोत्तम ..
चित्रगुप्तेश्वरंनाम विख्यातं भुवन त्रये .. 52 ..
17.16.m: A liṅga was also fashioned by him in that sacred field, O best of brahmins, / named Chitragupteśvara, famous in the three worlds. (52)

17.16.s:
paścimena cakāroccaiḥ prajāpatirudāradhīḥ ..
kedārākhyaṃ tadā liṃgaṃ girau raivatake sthitam ..
prajāpatiḥ svayaṃ tasthau tatra parvatasānuni .. 53 ..
17.16.d:
पश्चिमेन चकारोच्चैः प्रजापतिरुदारधीः ..
केदाराख्यं तदा लिंगं गिरौ रैवतके स्थितम् ..
प्रजापतिः स्वयं तस्थौ तत्र पर्वतसानुनि .. 53 ..
17.16.m: To the west, the noble-minded Prajāpati erected on high / the liṅga called Kedāra, situated on Mount Raivataka; / Prajāpati himself stood there on the mountain ridge. (53)

17.16.s:
.. rudra uvāca .. ..
iṃdreśvarasya māhātmyaṃ kathayiṣye śṛṇuṣva tat ..
īśānakoṇe vikhyātaṃ bhavasya viditaṃ mama .. 54 ..
17.16.d:
.. रुद्र उवाच .. ..
इंद्रेश्वरस्य माहात्म्यं कथयिष्ये शृणुष्व तत् ..
ईशानकोणे विख्यातं भवस्य विदितं मम .. 54 ..
17.16.m: Rudra said: / I shall narrate the māhātmya of Indreśvara; listen to it, / well-known in the north-eastern corner of Bhava, known to me. (54)

17.16.s:
..vāmana uvāca .. ..
kasmādiṃdraḥ samāyātaḥ kathaṃ cakre haraṃ hariḥ..
kathāṃ savistarāmetāṃ kathayasva mama prabho .. 55 ..
17.16.d:
..वामन उवाच .. ..
कस्मादिंद्रः समायातः कथं चक्रे हरं हरिः..
कथां सविस्तरामेतां कथयस्व मम प्रभो .. 55 ..
17.16.m: Vāmana said: / Why did Indra come, and how did Hari make Hara? / Narrate this story in full detail to me, O Lord. (55)

17.16.s:
.. rudra uvāca .. ..
lubdhakastu purā siddhaḥ śivarātriprajāgarāt ..
śivaloke tadā prāptaṃ vimānaṃ gaṇasaṃyutam .. 56 ..
17.16.d:
.. रुद्र उवाच .. ..
लुब्धकस्तु पुरा सिद्धः शिवरात्रिप्रजागरात् ..
शिवलोके तदा प्राप्तं विमानं गणसंयुतम् .. 56 ..
17.16.m: Rudra said: / Formerly, the hunter attained perfection through keeping vigil on Śivarātri. / Then an aerial chariot with attendants arrived from the world of Śiva; (56)

17.16.s: sarvatragaṃ suruciraṃ divyastrīgītanāditam .. tadāruhya samāyāto draṣṭuṃ tāṃ nagarīṃ hareḥ .. 57 ..
17.16.d: सर्वत्रगं सुरुचिरं दिव्यस्त्रीगीतनादितम् .. तदारुह्य समायातो द्रष्टुं तां नगरीं हरेः .. 57 ..
17.16.m: it travelled everywhere, very charming, resonant with songs of divine women. / Mounting it, he came to see that city of Hari, (57)

17.16.s:
yasyāṃ yuddhaṃ samabhavadgaṇānāṃ yamakiṃkaraiḥ ..
āgacchamānaṃ taṃ jñātvā devarājena ciṃtitam .. 58 ..
17.16.d:
यस्यां युद्धं समभवद्गणानां यमकिंकरैः ..
आगच्छमानं तं ज्ञात्वा देवराजेन चिंतितम् .. 58 ..
17.16.m: in which a battle had occurred between the attendants [of Śiva] and the servants of Yama. / Knowing that he was arriving, the king of gods thought: (58)

17.16.s:
pūjyo'yaṃ haravatsarvaiścitraguptayamādibhiḥ ..
iṃdro gajaṃ samāruhya mahiṣeṇa yamo yataḥ .. 59 ..
17.16.d:
पूज्योऽयं हरवत्सर्वैश्चित्रगुप्तयमादिभिः ..
इंद्रो गजं समारुह्य महिषेण यमो यतः .. 59 ..
17.16.m: "He must be worshipped like Hara by all, including Chitragupta and Yama." / Indra mounted his elephant, while Yama went on a buffalo. (59)

17.16.s:
vidhāya lekhanīṃ karṇe citragupto yamājñayā ..
tato hūtā gaṇāḥ sarve ye nītā dharaṇītalāt .. 7.2.16.60 ..
17.16.d:
विधाय लेखनीं कर्णे चित्रगुप्तो यमाज्ञया ..
ततो हूता गणाः सर्वे ये नीता धरणीतलात् .. 7.2.16.60 ..
17.16.m: Placing his pen behind his ear by the order of Yama, Chitragupta / then summoned all the attendants who had been brought from the surface of the earth. (60)

17.16.s:
nijāparādhasaṃtaptā gatāste dakṣiṇāmukham .. āthityapū
jā kartavyā lubdhake gṛhamāgate .. 61 ..
17.16.d:
निजापराधसंतप्ता गतास्ते दक्षिणामुखम् .. आथित्यपू
जा कर्तव्या लुब्धके गृहमागते .. 61 ..
17.16.m: Distressed by their own offense, they went facing south. / "Hospitable worship must be performed when the hunter comes to our home. (61)

17.16.s:
apūjite gate hyasminharo māṃ śapayiṣyati ..
tasmātpūjāṃ kariṣyāmi yathā tuṣyati śaṃkaraḥ .. 62 ..
17.16.d:
अपूजिते गते ह्यस्मिन्हरो मां शपयिष्यति ..
तस्मात्पूजां करिष्यामि यथा तुष्यति शंकरः .. 62 ..
17.16.m: Indeed, if he goes away unworshipped, Hara will curse me. / Therefore, I shall perform worship so that Śaṃkara is pleased." (62)

17.16.s:
devaṃ draṣṭuṃ samāyātaṃ dadarśādūrataḥ sthitam..
vimānasthaṃ harākāraṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham .. 63 ..
17.16.d:
देवं द्रष्टुं समायातं ददर्शादूरतः स्थितम्..
विमानस्थं हराकारं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् .. 63 ..
17.16.m: He beheld him who had come to see the god, stationed not far off, / mounted on an aerial chariot, having the form of Hara, brilliant as ten million suns, (63)

17.16.s:
saṃstūyamānaṃ caritaiḥ śivarātreḥ śivasya ca ..
māghe māse caturddaśyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ jāgare kṛte ..64..
17.16.d:
संस्तूयमानं चरितैः शिवरात्रेः शिवस्य च ..
माघे मासे चतुर्द्दश्यां कृष्णायां जागरे कृते ..64..
17.16.m: being praised with deeds of Śivarātri and of Śiva, / when vigil was kept on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight in the month of Māgha: (64)

17.16.s:
tadevaṃ jāyate sarvaṃ sureśvara dharātale ..
evaṃ devāṃganā kācidācakṣaṃtī puraṃdaram ..
nivārya hastamudyamya gajeṃdraṃ cārulocanā .. 65 ..
17.16.d:
तदेवं जायते सर्वं सुरेश्वर धरातले ..
एवं देवांगना काचिदाचक्षंती पुरंदरम् ..
निवार्य हस्तमुद्यम्य गजेंद्रं चारुलोचना .. 65 ..
17.16.m: "All this comes about in this way on the face of the earth, O Lord of the gods!" / Thus a certain celestial woman, declaring [this] to Purandara, / holding back the lordly elephant by raising her hand, she of beautiful eyes [said]: (65)

17.16.s:
kiṃ dānairbahubhirdattairvrataiḥ kiṃ kiṃ surārcanaiḥ ..
kiṃ yogaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiśca brahmacaryyaiḥ sureśvara .. 66 ..
17.16.d:
किं दानैर्बहुभिर्दत्तैर्व्रतैः किं किं सुरार्चनैः ..
किं योगैः किं तपोभिश्च ब्रह्मचर्य्यैः सुरेश्वर .. 66 ..
17.16.m: "What use are many gifts bestowed? What use are vows? What use are services to the gods? / What use are yogas, and what use are austerities and celibacies, O Lord of the gods? (66)

17.16.s:
gayāyāṃ piṃḍadānena prayāgamaraṇena kim ..
someśvare sarasvatyāṃ somaparvaṇi kiṃ gataiḥ .. 67 ..
17.16.d:
गयायां पिंडदानेन प्रयागमरणेन किम् ..
सोमेश्वरे सरस्वत्यां सोमपर्वणि किं गतैः .. 67 ..
17.16.m: What use is the offering of rice-balls at Gayā, or death at Prayāga? / What use is going to Someśvara on the Sarasvatī at the time of a lunar eclipse? (67)

17.16.s:
kurukṣetragataiḥ kiṃ syādrāhugraste divākare ..
tulāsuvarṇadānena vedapāṭhena kiṃ bhavet ..68..
17.16.d:
कुरुक्षेत्रगतैः किं स्याद्राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे ..
तुलासुवर्णदानेन वेदपाठेन किं भवेत् ..68..
17.16.m: What would come of going to Kurukṣetra when the sun is seized by Rāhu? / What would come of giving gold equal to one's weight, or of recitation of the Vedas? (68)

17.16.s:
sarvapāpakṣayo yena vṛṣotsargeṇa tena kim ..
godānaṃ kiṃ karotyevaṃ jaladānaṃ tathaiva ca .. 69 ..
17.16.d:
सर्वपापक्षयो येन वृषोत्सर्गेण तेन किम् ..
गोदानं किं करोत्येवं जलदानं तथैव च .. 69 ..
17.16.m: What of that release of a bull, by which all sins are destroyed? / What does the gift of a cow achieve in this way, and likewise the gift of water? (69)

17.16.s:
ayane viṣuve caiva saṃkrāṃtau kīdṛśaṃ phalam ..
māghamāse caturdaśyāṃ yādṛśaṃ jāgare kṛte .. 7.2.16.70 ..
17.16.d:
अयने विषुवे चैव संक्रांतौ कीदृशं फलम् ..
माघमासे चतुर्दश्यां यादृशं जागरे कृते .. 7.2.16.70 ..
17.16.m: What sort of fruit is there at the solstice, the equinox, or the transit of the sun, / compared to that which is attained when vigil is kept on the fourteenth in the month of Māgha?" (70)

17.16.s:
yamaḥ saṃbhāṣate vāṇyā mahiṣopari saṃsthitaḥ ..
paśya rudrasya māhātmyaṃ citragupta vicāraya .. 71 ..
17.16.d:
यमः संभाषते वाण्या महिषोपरि संस्थितः ..
पश्य रुद्रस्य माहात्म्यं चित्रगुप्त विचारय .. 71 ..
17.16.m: Seated upon his buffalo, Yama addressed [him] with these words: / "Look at the māhātmya of Rudra, Chitragupta; reflect upon it!" (71)

17.16.s:
ayaṃ sa lubdhako yena haraḥ saṃpūjitaḥ purā ..
surāṣṭradeśe vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ vastrāpathaṃ śṛṇu .. 72 ..
17.16.d:
अयं स लुब्धको येन हरः संपूजितः पुरा ..
सुराष्ट्रदेशे विख्यातं तीर्थं वस्त्रापथं शृणु .. 72 ..
17.16.m: "This is that hunter by whom Hara was worshipped long ago. / Listen about the sacred ford celebrated in the Surāṣṭra country as Vastrāpatha.

17.16.s:
ujjayaṃto giristatra tathā raivatako giriḥ ..
mahatī varttate jālistayormadhye mayā śrutam .. 73 ..
17.16.d:
उज्जयंतो गिरिस्तत्र तथा रैवतको गिरिः ..
महती वर्त्तते जालिस्तयोर्मध्ये मया श्रुतम् .. 73 ..
17.16.m: Mount Ujjayanta is there, and likewise Mount Raivataka. / Between them is a great thicket, as I have heard.

17.16.s:
mṛnmayaṃ vartate ligaṃ rātrau cānena pūjitaḥ ..
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ karttuṃ yena kāryeṇa cāgataḥ .. 74 ..
17.16.d:
मृन्मयं वर्तते लिगं रात्रौ चानेन पूजितः ..
रात्रौ जागरणं कर्त्तुं येन कार्येण चागतः .. 74 ..
17.16.m: There is an earthen liṅga, and he was worshipped at night by this [hunter], / who came for a certain purpose to keep a vigil at night.

17.16.s:
tadasmābhiḥ kathaṃ vācyaṃ svayaṃ jānaṃti te surāḥ ..
varāṃganā varaṃ draṣṭuṃ varayaṃti parasparam ..
iṃdrāvāsātsamāyātā naṃdane vegavattarāḥ .. 75 ..
17.16.d:
तदस्माभिः कथं वाच्यं स्वयं जानंति ते सुराः ..
वरांगना वरं द्रष्टुं वरयंति परस्परम् ..
इंद्रावासात्समायाता नंदने वेगवत्तराः .. 75 ..
17.16.m: How can that be spoken by us? The gods themselves know it." / Excellent women, desiring to see the chosen one, selected one another; / having come swiftly from Indra's abode to the Nandana garden,

17.16.s:
viraṃcinā rāyaṇaśaṃkaratviṣā dehena cāgacchati ko'pi pūruṣaḥ ..
purīṃ sureśādhipaternirīkṣituṃ bharttā mamāyaṃ tava cāsti kiṃ patiḥ .. 76 ..
17.16.d:
विरंचिना रायणशंकरत्विषा देहेन चागच्छति कोऽपि पूरुषः ..
पुरीं सुरेशाधिपतेर्निरीक्षितुं भर्त्ता ममायं तव चास्ति किं पतिः .. 76 ..
17.16.m: "A certain person is coming, possessing the splendor of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śaṃkara, / in bodily form, to see the city of the lord of the gods. Is this my husband, or is he your lord?"

17.16.s:
mṛdaṃgavīṇā paṭahasvarastutaiḥ pravodhitābhiḥ surarājamandire ..
devo haro'yaṃ na naro harākṛtirdṛṣṭoṃganābhistava kiṃ kimāvayoḥ .. 77 ..
17.16.d:
मृदंगवीणा पटहस्वरस्तुतैः प्रवोधिताभिः सुरराजमन्दिरे ..
देवो हरोऽयं न नरो हराकृतिर्दृष्टोंगनाभिस्तव किं किमावयोः .. 77 ..
17.16.m: Awakened in the palace of the king of gods by praises with the sounds of mṛdaṅgas, lute, and kettle-drums, / the women saw: "This god is Hara, not a mortal in the form of Hara. Is he yours? Or what, is he ours?"

17.16.s:
gāyaṃti kāścidvihasaṃti kāścinnṛtyaṃti kāścitprapaṭhaṃti kāścit ..
vadanti kāścijjayaśabdasaṃyutairvākyairanekairgurusannidhāne .. 78 ..
17.16.d:
गायंति काश्चिद्विहसंति काश्चिन्नृत्यंति काश्चित्प्रपठंति काश्चित् ..
वदन्ति काश्चिज्जयशब्दसंयुतैर्वाक्यैरनेकैर्गुरुसन्निधाने .. 78 ..
17.16.m: Some sing, some laugh, some dance, some recite aloud; / some speak with various words accompanied by shouts of 'Victory!' in the presence of the guru.

17.16.s:
kācicchivaṃ stauti śivāṃ tathānyā pṛcchatyathānyā kimu bilvapatrāt ..
kiṃ vopavāsena phalaṃ tavedaṃ nidrākṣayeṇātha phalaṃ tavaitat .. 79 ..
17.16.d:
काचिच्छिवं स्तौति शिवां तथान्या पृच्छत्यथान्या किमु बिल्वपत्रात् ..
किं वोपवासेन फलं तवेदं निद्राक्षयेणाथ फलं तवैतत् .. 79 ..
17.16.m: One praises Śiva, another praises Śivā; then another asks: "Is this fruit of yours from a bilva leaf, / or from fasting? Or is this fruit of yours from the loss of sleep?"

17.16.s:
tāsāṃ nānāvidhā vācaḥ śrūyante nandane vane ..
brahmalokādikā vārttāḥ kṛtvā ca tadanantaram .. 7.2.16.80 ..
17.16.d:
तासां नानाविधा वाचः श्रूयन्ते नन्दने वने ..
ब्रह्मलोकादिका वार्त्ताः कृत्वा च तदनन्तरम् .. 7.2.16.80 ..
17.16.m: Various words of theirs are heard in the Nandana grove. / And having engaged in conversations about Brahmā's world and others, thereafter

17.16.s:
devendro lubdhakaṃ bhūyo babhāṣe kautukānvitaḥ..
kasmindeśe girau jālirliṃgaṃ yatrāsti darśaya .. 81 ..
17.16.d:
देवेन्द्रो लुब्धकं भूयो बभाषे कौतुकान्वितः..
कस्मिन्देशे गिरौ जालिर्लिंगं यत्रास्ति दर्शय .. 81 ..
17.16.m: the lord of the gods, filled with curiosity, spoke again to the hunter: / "In which country, on which mountain is the thicket where the liṅga is? Show it [to me]."

17.16.s:
.. lubdhaka uvāca .. ..
surāṣṭradeśe vikhyāto yasmindeśe sarasvatī ..
vāḍavaṃ śirasā dhṛtvā praviṣṭā lavaṇodadhau .. 82 ..
17.16.d:
.. लुब्धक उवाच .. ..
सुराष्ट्रदेशे विख्यातो यस्मिन्देशे सरस्वती ..
वाडवं शिरसा धृत्वा प्रविष्टा लवणोदधौ .. 82 ..
17.16.m: The hunter said: / "In the famous country of Surāṣṭra, in which country the Sarasvatī, / bearing the submarine fire on her head, entered the salty ocean;

17.16.s:
yatra sā gomatī yāti yatrāste gandhamādanaḥ ..
ujjayaṃto girivaro yatra raivatako giriḥ .. 83 ..
17.16.d:
यत्र सा गोमती याति यत्रास्ते गन्धमादनः ..
उज्जयंतो गिरिवरो यत्र रैवतको गिरिः .. 83 ..
17.16.m: where that Gomatī flows, where Gandhamādana stands; / where Ujjayanta, the best of mountains, is, and where Mount Raivataka is;

17.16.s:
tatra vastrāpathaṃ kṣetraṃ bhavastatra vyavasthitaḥ ..
tatrāste mṛnmayaṃ liṃgaṃ jālimadhye surottama .. 84 ..
17.16.d:
तत्र वस्त्रापथं क्षेत्रं भवस्तत्र व्यवस्थितः ..
तत्रास्ते मृन्मयं लिंगं जालिमध्ये सुरोत्तम .. 84 ..
17.16.m: there is the sacred field Vastrāpatha; Bhava is situated there. / There stands the earthen liṅga in the midst of the thicket, O best of gods."

17.16.s:
.. indra uvāca .. ..
sahitaistatra gaṃtavyaṃ pūjayiṣye bhavaṃ svayam ..
jālimadhye tathā liṃgaṃ darśayasva ca lubdhaka .. 85 ..
17.16.d:
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
सहितैस्तत्र गंतव्यं पूजयिष्ये भवं स्वयम् ..
जालिमध्ये तथा लिंगं दर्शयस्व च लुब्धक .. 85 ..
17.16.m: Indra said: / "Together [with you] I must go there; I myself will worship Bhava. / And show me the liṅga in the midst of the thicket, O hunter.

17.16.s:
paradārādikaṃ pāpaṃ daityānāṃ tu vikṛṃtane ..
vadhe vṛtrasya saṃjātaṃ tatsarvaṃ kṣālayāmyaham .. 86 ..
17.16.d:
परदारादिकं पापं दैत्यानां तु विकृंतने ..
वधे वृत्रस्य संजातं तत्सर्वं क्षालयाम्यहम् .. 86 ..
17.16.m: The sin of touching another's wife and so on, incurred in destroying the Daityas / and in the slaying of Vṛtra—all that I will wash away."

17.16.s:
ityuktvā sahitāḥ sarve saṃprāptā girimūrddhani..
vāhanāni ca te tyaktvā prasthitāḥ pādacāriṇaḥ .. 87 ..
17.16.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सहिताः सर्वे संप्राप्ता गिरिमूर्द्धनि..
वाहनानि च ते त्यक्त्वा प्रस्थिताः पादचारिणः .. 87 ..
17.16.m: Having said this, all together reached the top of the mountain. / Leaving behind their vehicles, they set out on foot.

17.16.s:
ujjayantagirermūrdhni gajarājaḥ samāgataḥ ..
tadāgracaraṇaṃ tasya dadau mūrdhani kāraṇāt .. 88 ..
17.16.d:
उज्जयन्तगिरेर्मूर्ध्नि गजराजः समागतः ..
तदाग्रचरणं तस्य ददौ मूर्धनि कारणात् .. 88 ..
17.16.m: The king of elephants came to the peak of Mount Ujjayanta. / Then, for a specific purpose, he placed his forefoot upon its summit.

17.16.s:
tenākrānto girivarastoyaṃ susrāva nirmalam ..
gajapādodbhavaṃ vāri bhaviṣyati sadā sthiram .. 89 ..
17.16.d:
तेनाक्रान्तो गिरिवरस्तोयं सुस्राव निर्मलम् ..
गजपादोद्भवं वारि भविष्यति सदा स्थिरम् .. 89 ..
17.16.m: Pressed down by him, that best of mountains discharged pure water. / The water born from the elephant's foot will be permanent forever.

17.16.s:
iti proktaṃ surendreṇa lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā ..
sarve samāgatāstatra yatra jālirvyavasthitā .. 7.2.16.90 ..
17.16.d:
इति प्रोक्तं सुरेन्द्रेण लोकानां हितकाम्यया ..
सर्वे समागतास्तत्र यत्र जालिर्व्यवस्थिता .. 7.2.16.90 ..
17.16.m: Thus it was spoken by the lord of the gods, desiring the welfare of the worlds. / All of them arrived there, where the thicket was situated.

17.16.s:
saṃpūjya vividhaiḥ puṣpairmāghamāse caturdaśī ..
tasyāṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā sañjāto nirmalo hariḥ .. 91 ..
17.16.d:
संपूज्य विविधैः पुष्पैर्माघमासे चतुर्दशी ..
तस्यां जागरणं कृत्वा सञ्जातो निर्मलो हरिः .. 91 ..
17.16.m: Having worshipped with various flowers on the fourteenth day in the month of Māgha, / and having kept a vigil on it, Hari became pure.

17.16.s:
vastrāpathe bhavaṃ pūjya hariṃ raivatake girau ..
indreśvaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya saṃprāptaḥ svanikatanam.. 92 ..
17.16.d:
वस्त्रापथे भवं पूज्य हरिं रैवतके गिरौ ..
इन्द्रेश्वरं प्रतिष्ठाप्य संप्राप्तः स्वनिकतनम्.. 92 ..
17.16.m: Having worshipped Bhava at Vastrāpatha, and Hari on Mount Raivataka, / and having installed Indreśvara, he returned to his own abode.

17.16.s:
lubdhako'pi vimānena saṃprāpto harimandire ..
ityuktvā sa bhavo devastatraivāṃtaradhīyata .. 93 ..
17.16.d:
लुब्धकोऽपि विमानेन संप्राप्तो हरिमन्दिरे ..
इत्युक्त्वा स भवो देवस्तत्रैवांतरधीयत .. 93 ..
17.16.m: The hunter too reached the abode of Hari in an aerial chariot. / Having spoken thus, the god Bhava vanished right there.

17.16.s:
vāmanopi tataścakre tatra tīrthāvagāhanam ..
yādṛgrūpaḥ śivo dṛṣṭaḥ sūryabiṃbe digaṃbaraḥ .. 94 ..
17.16.d:
वामनोपि ततश्चक्रे तत्र तीर्थावगाहनम् ..
यादृग्रूपः शिवो दृष्टः सूर्यबिंबे दिगंबरः .. 94 ..
17.16.m: Then Vāmana also performed a plunge in the sacred ford there. / Just as Śiva was seen in the solar disc, space-clad,

17.16.s:
padmāsanasthitaḥ saumyastathā taṃ tatra saṃsmaran ..
pratiṣṭhāpya mahāmūrttiṃ pūjayāmāsa vāsaram .. 95 ..
17.16.d:
पद्मासनस्थितः सौम्यस्तथा तं तत्र संस्मरन् ..
प्रतिष्ठाप्य महामूर्त्तिं पूजयामास वासरम् .. 95 ..
17.16.m: seated in the lotus posture, tranquil, so remembering him there, / having installed the great form, he worshipped him for a day.

17.16.s:
mano'bhīṣṭārthasiddhyarthaṃ tataḥ siddhimavāptavān ..
nemināthaśivetyevaṃ nāma cakre sa vāmanaḥ .. 96..
17.16.d:
मनोऽभीष्टार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं ततः सिद्धिमवाप्तवान् ..
नेमिनाथशिवेत्येवं नाम चक्रे स वामनः .. 96..
17.16.m: For the sake of attaining the desired goal of his heart, he then obtained perfection. / That Vāmana gave it the name 'Neminātha-Śiva'.

17.16.s:
bhavasya paścime bhāge pratyāsanne dharātale ..
vāmano vasatiṃ cakre tīrthe vastrāpathe tadā .. 97 ..
17.16.d:
भवस्य पश्चिमे भागे प्रत्यासन्ने धरातले ..
वामनो वसतिं चक्रे तीर्थे वस्त्रापथे तदा .. 97 ..
17.16.m: In the western part of Bhava, nearby on the surface of the earth, / Vāmana then made his dwelling at the sacred ford Vastrāpatha.

17.16.s:
ato yavādhikaṃ proktaṃ tīrthaṃ devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ ..
iṃdreṇa kurvatā devaṃ samāgatya bhavāgrataḥ .. 98 ..
17.16.d:
अतो यवाधिकं प्रोक्तं तीर्थं देवैः सवासवैः ..
इंद्रेण कुर्वता देवं समागत्य भवाग्रतः .. 98 ..
17.16.m: Therefore the sacred ford is declared by the gods together with Indra to be greater by a barley-corn, / because Indra came before Bhava and worshipped the god.

17.16.s:
yavādhikaṃ prabhāsāttu tīrthametadbhavājñayā ..
anyeṣāṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ tīrthaṃ bhaviṣyati śivājñayā .. 99 ..
17.16.d:
यवाधिकं प्रभासात्तु तीर्थमेतद्भवाज्ञया ..
अन्येषां षड्गुणं तीर्थं भविष्यति शिवाज्ञया .. 99 ..
17.16.m: By the command of Bhava, this sacred ford is greater by a barley-corn than Prabhāsa. / By Śiva's command, it will be six times [greater than] other sacred fords.

17.16.s: ityetatkathitaṃ sarvaṃ kimanyatparipṛcchasi .. 7.2.16.100 .. ..
17.16.d: इत्येतत्कथितं सर्वं किमन्यत्परिपृच्छसि .. 7.2.16.100 .. ..
17.16.m: All this has been related; what else do you ask?"

17.16.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
śivarātriprabhāvoyamatulaḥ parikīrttitaḥ ..
ajānatā kṛtā tena lubdhakena purā śrutam .. 101 ..
17.16.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
शिवरात्रिप्रभावोयमतुलः परिकीर्त्तितः ..
अजानता कृता तेन लुब्धकेन पुरा श्रुतम् .. 101 ..
17.16.m: The king said: / "This power of Śivarātri has been described as incomparable. / Formerly it was heard [that it was] observed unknowingly by that hunter.

17.16.s:
idānīṃ vada karttavyā kathamanyairjanairvibho ..
kiṃ grāhyaṃ kiṃ nu moktavyaṃ śivarātryāṃ vadasva me .. 102 ..
17.16.d:
इदानीं वद कर्त्तव्या कथमन्यैर्जनैर्विभो ..
किं ग्राह्यं किं नु मोक्तव्यं शिवरात्र्यां वदस्व मे .. 102 ..
17.16.m: Now tell me, O lord, how is it to be observed by other men? / What is to be accepted, and what should be avoided on Śivarātri? Tell me."

17.16.s:
.. sārasvata uvāca .. ..
saṃprāpya mānuṣaṃ janma jñātvā devaṃ maheśvaram ..
śivarātriḥ sadā kāryā bhuktimuktipradāyinī .. 103 ..
17.16.d:
.. सारस्वत उवाच .. ..
संप्राप्य मानुषं जन्म ज्ञात्वा देवं महेश्वरम् ..
शिवरात्रिः सदा कार्या भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनी .. 103 ..
17.16.m: The Sārasvata said: / "Having attained human birth, and having known the god Maheśvara, / Śivarātri, which bestows enjoyment and liberation, must always be observed.

17.16.s:
īdṛśaṃ jāyate puṇyamekayā kṛtayā nṛpa ..
ye kurvaṃti sadā marttyāsteṣāṃ puṇyamanaṃtakam ..104 ..
17.16.d:
ईदृशं जायते पुण्यमेकया कृतया नृप ..
ये कुर्वंति सदा मर्त्त्यास्तेषां पुण्यमनंतकम् ..104 ..
17.16.m: Such religious merit arises from one [observance] performed, O king. / For those mortals who observe it always, their merit is endless.

17.16.s:
dvādaśābdaṃ vratamidaṃ karttavyaṃ prativatsaram..
jīvitaṃ caṃcalaṃ nṛṇāṃ yadi kartuṃ na śakyate .. 105 ..
17.16.d:
द्वादशाब्दं व्रतमिदं कर्त्तव्यं प्रतिवत्सरम्..
जीवितं चंचलं नृणां यदि कर्तुं न शक्यते .. 105 ..
17.16.m: This vow must be observed for twelve years, year after year. / If, because the life of men is fleeting, one is unable to do so,

17.16.s:
tadā dvādaśabhirmāsairvrata metatsamāpyate ..
māghamāse caturdaśyāṃ prārambhaḥ kriyate nṛpa .. 106 ..
17.16.d:
तदा द्वादशभिर्मासैर्व्रत मेतत्समाप्यते ..
माघमासे चतुर्दश्यां प्रारम्भः क्रियते नृप .. 106 ..
17.16.m: then this vow is completed in twelve months. / The commencement is made on the fourteenth day in the month of Māgha, O king.

17.16.s:
pratimāsaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ pauṣāṃte tu samāpyate ..
vighnaścejjāyate madhye kathaṃ ciddaivayogataḥ .. 107 ..
17.16.d:
प्रतिमासं ततः कार्यं पौषांते तु समाप्यते ..
विघ्नश्चेज्जायते मध्ये कथं चिद्दैवयोगतः .. 107 ..
17.16.m: Then it should be performed each month, and concludes at the end of Pauṣa. / If an obstacle should arise midway somehow through the working of destiny,

17.16.s:
na bhavedvratabhaṃgastu punaḥ kāryamanantaram ..
dvādaśaiva prakartavyāḥ kṛtvā saṃkhyā viśeṣataḥ .. 108 ..
17.16.d:
न भवेद्व्रतभंगस्तु पुनः कार्यमनन्तरम् ..
द्वादशैव प्रकर्तव्याः कृत्वा संख्या विशेषतः .. 108 ..
17.16.m: there will be no breach of the vow; it must be resumed immediately afterwards. / Keeping track of the count, twelve in all should definitely be performed.

17.16.s:
kṛtaṃ na naśyate loke śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham ..
kṛṣṇāyāṃ tu caturdaśyāṃ kṛtapūrvāhnikakriyaḥ .. 109 ..
17.16.d:
कृतं न नश्यते लोके शुभं वा यदि वाऽशुभम् ..
कृष्णायां तु चतुर्दश्यां कृतपूर्वाह्निकक्रियः .. 109 ..
17.16.m: What is done in this world does not perish, whether it is auspicious or inauspicious. / Having performed the morning rites on the dark fourteenth,

17.16.s:
upavāsaniyamo grāhyo nadyāṃ snānaṃ vidhīyate ..
tadabhāve taḍāgādau kāryaṃ snānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ .. 7.2.16.110 ..
17.16.d:
उपवासनियमो ग्राह्यो नद्यां स्नानं विधीयते ..
तदभावे तडागादौ कार्यं स्नानं स्वशक्तितः .. 7.2.16.110 ..
17.16.m: the rule of fasting must be undertaken, and ritual ablution in a river is prescribed. / In the absence of that, one should perform a ritual ablution according to one's capacity in a pond or the like.

17.16.s:
tailābhyaṃgo na karttavyo na kāryaṃ gamanaṃ kvacit ..
tīrthasevā prakarttavyā tasmiṃścāgamanaṃ śubham .. 111 ..
17.16.d:
तैलाभ्यंगो न कर्त्तव्यो न कार्यं गमनं क्वचित् ..
तीर्थसेवा प्रकर्त्तव्या तस्मिंश्चागमनं शुभम् .. 111 ..
17.16.m: Rubbing with oil should not be done, nor should any travel be undertaken anywhere. / Service to a sacred ford should be performed, and arriving there is auspicious.

17.16.s:
śivarātriḥ sadā kāryā liṃge svāyaṃbhuve naraiḥ ..
tadabhāve mahāpuṇye liṃge varṣaśatādhike .. 112 ..
17.16.d:
शिवरात्रिः सदा कार्या लिंगे स्वायंभुवे नरैः ..
तदभावे महापुण्ये लिंगे वर्षशताधिके .. 112 ..
17.16.m: Śivarātri must always be observed by men at a self-manifest liṅga; / in the absence of that, at a highly meritorious liṅga older than a hundred years."

17.16.s:
girau vane samudrāṃte nadyāṃ yacca śivālaye ..
tadvai svāyaṃbhuvaṃ liṃgaṃ svayaṃ tatraiva saṃsthitam .. 113 ..
17.16.d:
गिरौ वने समुद्रांते नद्यां यच्च शिवालये ..
तद्वै स्वायंभुवं लिंगं स्वयं तत्रैव संस्थितम् .. 113 ..
17.16.m: A liṅga that is on a mountain, in a forest, by the sea, in a river, or in an abode of Śiva, / is indeed a self-manifest liṅga, situated there by itself.

17.16.s:
vāluliṃgādikaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjitaṃ phaladaṃ smṛtam ..
divā saṃpūjya yatnena puṣpadhūpādinā naraḥ .. 114 ..
17.16.d:
वालुलिंगादिकं लिंगं पूजितं फलदं स्मृतम् ..
दिवा संपूज्य यत्नेन पुष्पधूपादिना नरः .. 114 ..
17.16.m: A liṅga made of sand and the like, when worshipped, is traditionally held to yield fruits. / Having worshipped it diligently by day with flowers, incense, and other offerings, a man,

17.16.s:
varjayenmadirāṃ dyūtaṃ nārīṃ nakhanikṛntanam ..
brahmacaryaparaiḥ śāṃtaiḥ karttavyaṃ samupoṣaṇam .. 115 ..
17.16.d:
वर्जयेन्मदिरां द्यूतं नारीं नखनिकृन्तनम् ..
ब्रह्मचर्यपरैः शांतैः कर्त्तव्यं समुपोषणम् .. 115 ..
17.16.m: Should avoid liquor, gambling, women, and the clipping of nails. / Dedicated to celibacy and tranquil, [such people] must observe the fast.

17.16.s:
rātrau devāgrato gatvā karttavyāḥ sapta parvatāḥ ..
pakvānnaphalatāṃbūlapuṣpadhūpādicarcitāḥ .. 116 ..
17.16.d:
रात्रौ देवाग्रतो गत्वा कर्त्तव्याः सप्त पर्वताः ..
पक्वान्नफलतांबूलपुष्पधूपादिचर्चिताः .. 116 ..
17.16.m: Going before the deity at night, seven mountains should be made, / smeared with cooked food, fruits, betel, flowers, incense, and the like.

17.16.s:
ghṛtena dīpaḥ karttavyaḥ pāpanāśanahetave ..
yato dīpasya māhātmyaṃ vijñeyaṃ muktidāyakam .. 117 ..
17.16.d:
घृतेन दीपः कर्त्तव्यः पापनाशनहेतवे ..
यतो दीपस्य माहात्म्यं विज्ञेयं मुक्तिदायकम् .. 117 ..
17.16.m: A lamp with ghee should be prepared for the purpose of destroying sin, / for the māhātmya of the lamp is to be known as bestowing liberation.

17.16.s:
dīpaḥ sadaiva karttavyo gṛhe devālaye naraiḥ ..
divā niśi ca saṃdhyāyāṃ dīpaḥ kāryaḥ svaśaktitaḥ .. 118 ..
17.16.d:
दीपः सदैव कर्त्तव्यो गृहे देवालये नरैः ..
दिवा निशि च संध्यायां दीपः कार्यः स्वशक्तितः .. 118 ..
17.16.m: A lamp should always be maintained by men in the home and in a temple; / by day, by night, and at twilight, a lamp is to be made according to one's ability.

17.16.s:
kiñciduddyotamātreṇa devāstuṣyaṃti bhūtale ..
pitṝṇāṃ prathamaṃ dīpaḥ karttavyaḥ śrāddhakarmaṇi .. 119 ..
17.16.d:
किञ्चिदुद्द्योतमात्रेण देवास्तुष्यंति भूतले ..
पितॄणां प्रथमं दीपः कर्त्तव्यः श्राद्धकर्मणि .. 119 ..
17.16.m: By mere slight illumination, the gods on the earth are pleased. / First, a lamp must be made for the ancestors in the śrāddha rite.

17.16.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ yathā nidrā na jā yate ..
śivarātriprabhāvo'yaṃ śrotavyaḥ śivasaṃnidhau .. 7.2.16.120 ..
17.16.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कार्यं यथा निद्रा न जा यते ..
शिवरात्रिप्रभावोऽयं श्रोतव्यः शिवसंनिधौ .. 7.2.16.120 ..
17.16.m: A vigil should be kept at night so that sleep does not occur. / This power of Śivarātri should be listened to in the presence of Śiva.

17.16.s:
śivasya caritaṃ rātrau śrotavyaṃ bahuvistaram ..
gītaṃ nṛtyaṃ tathā vādyaṃ kartavyaṃ śivasaṃnidhau .. 121 ..
17.16.d:
शिवस्य चरितं रात्रौ श्रोतव्यं बहुविस्तरम् ..
गीतं नृत्यं तथा वाद्यं कर्तव्यं शिवसंनिधौ .. 121 ..
17.16.m: The deeds of Śiva should be listened to in great detail at night; / song, dance, and instrumental music should likewise be performed in the presence of Śiva.

17.16.s:
evaṃ sā nīyate rātrirmukhyaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ yataḥ ..
rātrau deyāni dānāni śaktyā vai tatra jāgare .. 122 ..
17.16.d:
एवं सा नीयते रात्रिर्मुख्यं जागरणं यतः ..
रात्रौ देयानि दानानि शक्त्या वै तत्र जागरे .. 122 ..
17.16.m: In this way that night is spent, for keeping vigil is primary; / gifts should indeed be given according to one's capacity at night during that vigil.

17.16.s:
punaḥ snātvā prabhāte tu karttavyaṃ śivapūjanam ..
pūjanīyāśca yatayo bhojanācchādanādibhiḥ .. 123 ..
17.16.d:
पुनः स्नात्वा प्रभाते तु कर्त्तव्यं शिवपूजनम् ..
पूजनीयाश्च यतयो भोजनाच्छादनादिभिः .. 123 ..
17.16.m: Having bathed again at dawn, the worship of Śiva is to be performed; / and ascetics should be honoured with food, clothing, and the like.

17.16.s:
tapasvināṃ pradātavyaṃ bhojanaṃ gṛhamedhibhiḥ ..
dvādaśāṣṭau ca catvāro bhoktavyā eka eva vā .. 124 ..
17.16.d:
तपस्विनां प्रदातव्यं भोजनं गृहमेधिभिः ..
द्वादशाष्टौ च चत्वारो भोक्तव्या एक एव वा .. 124 ..
17.16.m: Food should be given to practitioners of tapas by householders; / twelve, eight, four, or even just one should be fed.

17.16.s:
eko'pi brahmacārī yo brahmavicchivapūjakaḥ ..
sahasrāṇāṃ samo bhaktyā gṛhe saṃbhojito bhavet .. 125 ...
17.16.d:
एकोऽपि ब्रह्मचारी यो ब्रह्मविच्छिवपूजकः ..
सहस्राणां समो भक्त्या गृहे संभोजितो भवेत् .. 125 ...
17.16.m: Even a single celibate student who knows Brahman and worships Śiva, / when fed with devotion in the house, is equal to thousands.

17.16.s:
akṣārālavaṇaṃ patre bhoktavyaṃ vāgyataiḥ svayam ..
putramitrakalatrāṇāṃ dātavyaṃ bhojanaṃ puraḥ .. 126 ..
17.16.d:
अक्षारालवणं पत्रे भोक्तव्यं वाग्यतैः स्वयम् ..
पुत्रमित्रकलत्राणां दातव्यं भोजनं पुरः .. 126 ..
17.16.m: One should oneself eat food on a leaf without alkaline or salt, restraining speech, / having first given food to sons, friends, and wives.

17.16.s:
anena vidhinā kāryā śivarātriḥ śivavrataiḥ ..
dvādaśaitā yadā pūrṇāstilapātrāṇi vai tadā .. 127 ..
17.16.d:
अनेन विधिना कार्या शिवरात्रिः शिवव्रतैः ..
द्वादशैता यदा पूर्णास्तिलपात्राणि वै तदा .. 127 ..
17.16.m: According to this rite Śivarātri is to be observed by those observing the vow of Śiva. / When these twelve are completed, then vessels of sesame seeds

17.16.s:
dvādaśaiva pradeyānigurubrāhmaṇajñātiṣu ..
vratāṃte gauḥ pradātavyā kṛṣṇā vatsayutā dṛḍhā ..128..
17.16.d:
द्वादशैव प्रदेयानिगुरुब्राह्मणज्ञातिषु ..
व्रतांते गौः प्रदातव्या कृष्णा वत्सयुता दृढा ..128..
17.16.m: —twelve indeed—should be given to the guru, brahmins, and kinsmen. / At the conclusion of the vow, a cow should be given: black, with its calf, and sturdy,

17.16.s:
savastrābharaṇā deyā ghaṃṭābharaṇabhūṣitā ..
aṃgulīyakavāsāṃsi cchatropānatkamaṇḍalu .. 129 ..
17.16.d:
सवस्त्राभरणा देया घंटाभरणभूषिता ..
अंगुलीयकवासांसि च्छत्रोपानत्कमण्डलु .. 129 ..
17.16.m: Endowed with garments and ornaments, adorned with bell-ornaments, / [along with] a ring, clothes, an umbrella, sandals, and a water-pot.

17.16.s:
gurave dakṣiṇā deyābrāhmaṇebhyaḥ svaśaktitaḥ ..
evaṃ kṛtvā tato deyaṃ tapasvibhyo'tha bhojanam ..
miṣṭānnaṃ vividhaṃ dattvā kṣamāpya ca visarjayet .. 7.2.16.130 ..
17.16.d:
गुरवे दक्षिणा देयाब्राह्मणेभ्यः स्वशक्तितः ..
एवं कृत्वा ततो देयं तपस्विभ्योऽथ भोजनम् ..
मिष्टान्नं विविधं दत्त्वा क्षमाप्य च विसर्जयेत् .. 7.2.16.130 ..
17.16.m: A sacrificial fee should be given to the guru, and to the brahmins according to one's ability. / Having done this, food should then be given to the ascetics; / having given various sweet dishes and asked their forgiveness, one should dismiss them.

17.16.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute satyaṃ tasya pāpaṃ na vidyate ..
saṃtānamuttamaṃ labdhvā bhuktvā bhogānanuttamān.. 131 ..
17.16.d:
एवं यः कुरुते सत्यं तस्य पापं न विद्यते ..
संतानमुत्तमं लब्ध्वा भुक्त्वा भोगाननुत्तमान्.. 131 ..
17.16.m: For one who truly acts thus, no sin exists; / having obtained excellent offspring and enjoyed unsurpassed pleasures,

17.16.s:
divyavimānamārūḍho divyastrīpariveṣṭitaḥ ..
gativāditranirghoṣairnīyate śivamandire..132..
17.16.d:
दिव्यविमानमारूढो दिव्यस्त्रीपरिवेष्टितः ..
गतिवादित्रनिर्घोषैर्नीयते शिवमन्दिरे..132..
17.16.m: Mounted on a celestial aerial chariot, surrounded by celestial women, / he is led to the temple of Śiva with the resounding sounds of motion and musical instruments.

17.16.s:
tadetatkathitaṃ puṇyaṃ śivarātrivrataṃ mayā ..
kṛtena yena lokānāṃ sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet .. 133 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye śivarātrimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 16 ..
17.16.d:
तदेतत्कथितं पुण्यं शिवरात्रिव्रतं मया ..
कृतेन येन लोकानां सर्वपापक्षयो भवेत् .. 133 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शिवरात्रिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम षोडशोऽध्यायः .. 16 ..
17.16.m:
This meritorious vow of Śivarātri has thus been told by me, / through the performance of which the destruction of all sins occurs for men.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Śivarātri', in the second [sub-section], the Vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmya, of the seventh section, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

17.17.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
vicitramidamākhyānaṃ tvatprasādācchrutaṃ mayā ..
dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ śakraṃ nārado maṃdare girau .. 1 ..
17.17.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
विचित्रमिदमाख्यानं त्वत्प्रसादाच्छ्रुतं मया ..
दृष्ट्वा नारायणं शक्रं नारदो मंदरे गिरौ .. 1 ..
17.17.m: The king said: / Wonderful is this narrative heard by me through your grace. / Having seen Nārāyaṇa and Śakra on Mount Mandara,

17.17.s:
kiṃ cakāra munīṃdro'tha tanme vistarato mune ..
vada saṃsārasaraṇodbhūtamāyāprapīḍitam ..
kathāmṛtajalaughena vitṛṣaṃ kuru māṃ prabho .. 2 ..
17.17.d:
किं चकार मुनींद्रोऽथ तन्मे विस्तरतो मुने ..
वद संसारसरणोद्भूतमायाप्रपीडितम् ..
कथामृतजलौघेन वितृषं कुरु मां प्रभो .. 2 ..
17.17.m: What did the lord of sages do then? Tell me that in detail, O sage! / Make me, who am tormented by the delusion arising from wandering in saṃsāra, / free of thirst by the flood of the nectar-water of the narrative, O lord!

17.17.s:
.. sārasvata uvāca .. ..
athāsau nārado devaṃ jñātvā śaptaṃ dvijanmanā ..
bhṛguṇā ca tathā pūrvaṃ nānyathaitadbhaviṣyati .. 3 ..
17.17.d:
.. सारस्वत उवाच .. ..
अथासौ नारदो देवं ज्ञात्वा शप्तं द्विजन्मना ..
भृगुणा च तथा पूर्वं नान्यथैतद्भविष्यति .. 3 ..
17.17.m: The Sārasvata [sage] said: / Then that Nārada, knowing that the god had been cursed previously by the twice-born / Bhṛgu, [thought:] 'This will not happen otherwise.

17.17.s:
bhaviṣyaṃ yadbhavaṃ deva vartamānaṃ viciṃtyatām ..
ayaṃ ca vāmano bhūtvā viṣṇuryāsyati tāṃ purīm .. 4 ..
17.17.d:
भविष्यं यद्भवं देव वर्तमानं विचिंत्यताम् ..
अयं च वामनो भूत्वा विष्णुर्यास्यति तां पुरीम् .. 4 ..
17.17.m: What is to happen, will happen, O Lord; let the present be considered! / And this Viṣṇu, having become Vāmana, will go to that city.

17.17.s:
nigrahaṃ sa baleḥ paścātkariṣyati mama priyam ..
yuddhaṃ vinā kathaṃ stheyaṃ vartamānaṃ maholbaṇam .. 5 ..
17.17.d:
निग्रहं स बलेः पश्चात्करिष्यति मम प्रियम् ..
युद्धं विना कथं स्थेयं वर्तमानं महोल्बणम् .. 5 ..
17.17.m: Afterward he will subdue Bali, which will please me. / How can one remain in the present, fierce [state of affairs] without a war?

17.17.s:
devadānavayuddhāni daityagandharva rakṣasām ..
nivāritāni sarvāṇi sarīsṛpapatatriṇām .. 6 ..
17.17.d:
देवदानवयुद्धानि दैत्यगन्धर्व रक्षसाम् ..
निवारितानि सर्वाणि सरीसृपपतत्रिणाम् .. 6 ..
17.17.m: The battles between gods and dānavas, of daityas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas, / of reptiles and birds—all have been stopped.

17.17.s:
sāpatnajaḥ kalirnāsti mama bhāgyaparikṣaye ..
devendro guruṇā pūrvaṃ vāritaḥ kiṃ karomyaham .. 7 ..
17.17.d:
सापत्नजः कलिर्नास्ति मम भाग्यपरिक्षये ..
देवेन्द्रो गुरुणा पूर्वं वारितः किं करोम्यहम् .. 7 ..
17.17.m: In the destruction of my fortune, there is no strife born of rivalry. / The lord of the gods was previously restrained by his guru; what shall I do?

17.17.s:
mānanīyo gururme'yamatastaṃ na śapāmyaham ..
yuddhārthaṃ tu tato yatno na sidhyati karomi kim .. 8 ..
17.17.d:
माननीयो गुरुर्मेऽयमतस्तं न शपाम्यहम् ..
युद्धार्थं तु ततो यत्नो न सिध्यति करोमि किम् .. 8 ..
17.17.m: This guru is to be respected by me, so I do not curse him. / But then my effort for war does not succeed; what do I do?

17.17.s:
kenāpi daivayogena puruṣārtho na sidhyati ..
tathāpi yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ puruṣārthe vipaścitā ..
daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa vināpi phalati kvacit .. 9 ..
17.17.d:
केनापि दैवयोगेन पुरुषार्थो न सिध्यति ..
तथापि यत्नः कर्तव्यः पुरुषार्थे विपश्चिता ..
दैवं पुरुषकारेण विनापि फलति क्वचित् .. 9 ..
17.17.m: By some stroke of fate, human effort does not succeed; / even so, effort should be made towards human endeavor by a wise man. / Fate sometimes bears fruit even without human effort—

17.17.s:
yaduktaṃ tadvaco vyarthaṃ yataḥ siddhiḥ prayatnataḥ ..
baliṃ gatvā bhaṇiṣyāmi yathā yuddhaṃ kariṣyati .. 7.2.17.10 ..
17.17.d:
यदुक्तं तद्वचो व्यर्थं यतः सिद्धिः प्रयत्नतः ..
बलिं गत्वा भणिष्यामि यथा युद्धं करिष्यति .. 7.2.17.10 ..
17.17.m: That statement which has been said is useless, since success comes from exertion. / Having gone to Bali, I shall speak so that he will wage war.

17.17.s:
na śroṣyati sa cedvākyaṃ niścitaṃ taṃ śapāmyaham ..
ityuktvā sa yayau vegānnārado balimaṃdire ..
nimeṣāṃtaramātreṇa śiṣyābhyāṃ gagane sthitaḥ .. 11 ..
17.17.d:
न श्रोष्यति स चेद्वाक्यं निश्चितं तं शपाम्यहम् ..
इत्युक्त्वा स ययौ वेगान्नारदो बलिमंदिरे ..
निमेषांतरमात्रेण शिष्याभ्यां गगने स्थितः .. 11 ..
17.17.m: If he does not listen to my word, I shall certainly curse him.' / Having spoken thus, Nārada swiftly went to the palace of Bali; / in merely the twinkling of an eye, he stood in the sky with his two disciples.

17.17.s:
prāsāde śailasaṃkāśe saptabhaume mahojjvale ..
tasyopari sabhā divyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā .. 12 ..
17.17.d:
प्रासादे शैलसंकाशे सप्तभौमे महोज्ज्वले ..
तस्योपरि सभा दिव्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा .. 12 ..
17.17.m: Upon a mansion resembling a mountain, seven stories high and exceedingly bright, / on top of it was a celestial assembly hall fashioned by Viśvakarman.

17.17.s:
tasyāṃ siṃhāsanaṃ divyaṃ tatrāsīno balirnṛpa ..
daityaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvaiḥ prauḍhihāsyakathāparaiḥ .. 13 ..
17.17.d:
तस्यां सिंहासनं दिव्यं तत्रासीनो बलिर्नृप ..
दैत्यैः परिवृतः सर्वैः प्रौढिहास्यकथापरैः .. 13 ..
17.17.m: In it was a celestial lion-throne; seated upon it was Bali, O king, / surrounded by all the daityas, who were devoted to proud talk and laughter,

17.17.s:
ṛṣibhirbrāhmaṇaiḥ śāṃtaista thaivośanasā svayam..
putramitrakalatraiśca saṃvṛto divyamandire .. 14 ..
17.17.d:
ऋषिभिर्ब्राह्मणैः शांतैस्त थैवोशनसा स्वयम्..
पुत्रमित्रकलत्रैश्च संवृतो दिव्यमन्दिरे .. 14 ..
17.17.m: Surrounded by calm seers and brahmins, and likewise by Uśanas himself, / and by sons, friends, and wives, in the celestial palace.

17.17.s:
devāṃganākaragrāhagṛhītairdivyacāmaraiḥ ..
saṃvījyamāno daityendraḥ stūyamānaḥ sa cāraṇaiḥ .. 15 ..
17.17.d:
देवांगनाकरग्राहगृहीतैर्दिव्यचामरैः ..
संवीज्यमानो दैत्येन्द्रः स्तूयमानः स चारणैः .. 15 ..
17.17.m: The lord of the daityas was fanned with celestial chowries held by the hands of heavenly nymphs, / and was being praised by cāraṇas.

17.17.s:
yāvadāste madonmattā mantrayaṃti parasparam ..
daityadānavamukhyā ye te sarve yuddhakāṃkṣiṇaḥ .. 16 ..
17.17.d:
यावदास्ते मदोन्मत्ता मन्त्रयंति परस्परम् ..
दैत्यदानवमुख्या ये ते सर्वे युद्धकांक्षिणः .. 16 ..
17.17.m: While he was seated, intoxicated with arrogance, those chiefs of the daityas and dānavas, / who were all eager for battle, were deliberating among themselves.

17.17.s:
utthāyotthāya bhāṣaṃte pragalbhaṃte suraiḥ saha ..
asmadīyamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sāṃprataṃ gatam .. 17 ..
17.17.d:
उत्थायोत्थाय भाषंते प्रगल्भंते सुरैः सह ..
अस्मदीयमिदं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सांप्रतं गतम् .. 17 ..
17.17.m: Rising again and again, they spoke, boasting against the gods: / 'All this triple world of ours has now departed!

17.17.s:
śukrabuddhyā vinā yuddhaṃ prāpsyate kiṃ mahodayaḥ ..
daityendro devarājena snehaṃ ca kuruto yadi .. 18 ..
17.17.d:
शुक्रबुद्ध्या विना युद्धं प्राप्स्यते किं महोदयः ..
दैत्येन्द्रो देवराजेन स्नेहं च कुरुतो यदि .. 18 ..
17.17.m: Through Śukra's advice, will great prosperity be obtained without a war? / If the lord of daityas makes friendship with the king of the gods,

17.17.s:
airāvaṇaṃ sadā mattaṃ kathaṃ no yācate baliḥ ..
caturaṃ turagaṃ kasmānnārpayati divākaraḥ .. 19 ..
17.17.d:
ऐरावणं सदा मत्तं कथं नो याचते बलिः ..
चतुरं तुरगं कस्मान्नार्पयति दिवाकरः .. 19 ..
17.17.m: Why does Bali not ask for Airāvaṇa, who is always rutting? / Why does the Sun not surrender his swift horse?'

17.17.s:
yāvannākramyate lubdho dhanādhyakṣo raṇājire ..
tāvannārpayate vittaṃ yadā tatsaṃcitaṃ suraiḥ .. 7.2.17.20 ..
17.17.d:
यावन्नाक्रम्यते लुब्धो धनाध्यक्षो रणाजिरे ..
तावन्नार्पयते वित्तं यदा तत्संचितं सुरैः .. 7.2.17.20 ..
17.17.m: As long as the greedy treasurer is not attacked on the battlefield, / so long will he not surrender the wealth that was accumulated by the gods.

17.17.s:
na darśayati ratnāni jalarāśī rasātalāt ..
yāvanna mandaraṃ kṣiptvā vimathnīmo vayaṃ ca tam .. 21 ..
17.17.d:
न दर्शयति रत्नानि जलराशी रसातलात् ..
यावन्न मन्दरं क्षिप्त्वा विमथ्नीमो वयं च तम् .. 21 ..
17.17.m: The ocean does not reveal its jewels from the netherworld, / as long as we do not cast Mandara into it and churn it.

17.17.s:
yathāmṛtakalāścandrādbhujyante kramaśaḥ suraiḥ ..
evaṃ bhāgaṃ baleḥ kasmānna dadāti jalātmakaḥ .. 22 ..
17.17.d:
यथामृतकलाश्चन्द्राद्भुज्यन्ते क्रमशः सुरैः ..
एवं भागं बलेः कस्मान्न ददाति जलात्मकः .. 22 ..
17.17.m: Just as the digits of nectar from the moon are consumed gradually by the gods, / why does the watery one not give a share to Bali?

17.17.s:
svardhunī śītalo vātaḥ padmarkijalkavāsitaḥ ..
svarge vāti śanairyadvattathā na balimaṃdire .. 23 ..
17.17.d:
स्वर्धुनी शीतलो वातः पद्मर्किजल्कवासितः ..
स्वर्गे वाति शनैर्यद्वत्तथा न बलिमंदिरे .. 23 ..
17.17.m: The cool wind of the celestial river, fragrant with lotus filaments, / blows gently in heaven, but not likewise in the palace of Bali.

17.17.s:
indracāpodyatā meghā jalaṃ muṃcaṃti bhūtale..
balikhaṅgoddhutāḥ svargaṃ punaste yāṃti bhūtalāt..24..
17.17.d:
इन्द्रचापोद्यता मेघा जलं मुंचंति भूतले..
बलिखङ्गोद्धुताः स्वर्गं पुनस्ते यांति भूतलात्..24..
17.17.m: Clouds uplifted with rainbows release water upon the earth's surface; / shaken by Bali’s sword, they go again from the surface of the earth to heaven.

17.17.s:
asmadīye dharāpṛṣṭhe yamo mārayate janam ..
naivaṃ svarge na pātāle paśyāho kāryakāraṇam ..25..
17.17.d:
अस्मदीये धरापृष्ठे यमो मारयते जनम् ..
नैवं स्वर्गे न पाताले पश्याहो कार्यकारणम् ..25..
17.17.m: On our earthly surface, Yama kills people; / it is not so in heaven, nor in Pātāla—behold, alas, this cause and effect!

17.17.s:
āyurvṛttiṃ sutānsaukhyamasmākaṃ likhati svayam ..
lalāṭe citragupto'sau na devānāṃ tu tatsamam ..26..
17.17.d:
आयुर्वृत्तिं सुतान्सौख्यमस्माकं लिखति स्वयम् ..
ललाटे चित्रगुप्तोऽसौ न देवानां तु तत्समम् ..26..
17.17.m: That Citragupta personally writes upon our foreheads / lifespan, livelihood, sons, and happiness; but for the gods, it is not the same.

17.17.s:
varṣāśītātapāḥ kālā vartaṃte bhuvi sāṃpratam ..
na svarge naiva pātāle bhītā bhūmau bhramaṃti hi .. 27 ..
17.17.d:
वर्षाशीतातपाः काला वर्तंते भुवि सांप्रतम् ..
न स्वर्गे नैव पाताले भीता भूमौ भ्रमंति हि .. 27 ..
17.17.m: The seasons of rain, cold, and heat exist now upon the earth; / they wander upon the earth in fear, not in heaven nor in Pātāla.

17.17.s:
ekavīryodbhavā yūyaṃ svasrīyā devadānavāḥ ..
bhūmau sthitā vayaṃ kasmāddevāḥ kenoparikṛtāḥ .. ..28..
17.17.d:
एकवीर्योद्भवा यूयं स्वस्रीया देवदानवाः ..
भूमौ स्थिता वयं कस्माद्देवाः केनोपरिकृताः .. ..28..
17.17.m: Born from one seed, you gods and Dānavas are cousins; / why are we placed on earth, and by whom are the gods placed above?

17.17.s:
samudre mathyamāne tu daityendro vaṃcitaḥ suraiḥ ..
ekataḥ sarvadevāśca baliścaivaikataḥ sthitaḥ ..29..
17.17.d:
समुद्रे मथ्यमाने तु दैत्येन्द्रो वंचितः सुरैः ..
एकतः सर्वदेवाश्च बलिश्चैवैकतः स्थितः ..29..
17.17.m: When the ocean was being churned, the king of Daityas was deceived by the gods; / all the gods stood on one side, and Bali alone stood on the other.

17.17.s:
utpanneṣu ca ratneṣu bhāgyaṃ vai yasya yādṛśam ..
gajāśvakalpavṛkṣādyāścaṃdragogaṇadaṃtinaḥ ..7.2.17.30..
17.17.d:
उत्पन्नेषु च रत्नेषु भाग्यं वै यस्य यादृशम् ..
गजाश्वकल्पवृक्षाद्याश्चंद्रगोगणदंतिनः ..7.2.17.30..
17.17.m: And when the jewels emerged—whatever anyone's fortune was: / elephants, horses, wish-fulfilling trees, the moon, cows, and celestial tuskers.

17.17.s:
gṛhītvā hyamṛtaṃ devairvayaṃ pāne niyojitāḥ ..
etayā cūrṇitā yūyaṃ na jānīthātigarvitāḥ .. 31 ..
17.17.d:
गृहीत्वा ह्यमृतं देवैर्वयं पाने नियोजिताः ..
एतया चूर्णिता यूयं न जानीथातिगर्विताः .. 31 ..
17.17.m: Taking the nectar, the gods assigned us to drinking [liquor]; / crushed by this, you, exceedingly arrogant, do not know.

17.17.s:
pītāvaśeṣaṃ pīyūṣaṃ satyaloke dhṛtaṃ suraiḥ ..
ahotikuṭilā devāḥ kasmāccheṣaṃ na dīyate .. 32 ..
17.17.d:
पीतावशेषं पीयूषं सत्यलोके धृतं सुरैः ..
अहोतिकुटिला देवाः कस्माच्छेषं न दीयते .. 32 ..
17.17.m: The remaining nectar that was not drunk was kept by the gods in Satyaloka; / ah, how crooked are the gods! Why is the remainder not given?

17.17.s:
surāmṛtamiti jñātvā pīyūṣādvaṃcitā vayam ..
tilatailamevamiṣṭaṃ yairna dṛṣṭaṃ ghṛtaṃ kvacit.. 33 ..
17.17.d:
सुरामृतमिति ज्ञात्वा पीयूषाद्वंचिता वयम् ..
तिलतैलमेवमिष्टं यैर्न दृष्टं घृतं क्वचित्.. 33 ..
17.17.m: Believing it to be wine, we were deceived of the nectar; / thus sesame oil is dear to those who have never seen clarified butter.

17.17.s:
viṣṇorvakracaritrāṇāṃ saṃkhyā kartu na śakyate..
tathāpi kathyate tuṣṭairhṛṣṭaistairyadanuṣṭhitam ..34..
17.17.d:
विष्णोर्वक्रचरित्राणां संख्या कर्तु न शक्यते..
तथापि कथ्यते तुष्टैर्हृष्टैस्तैर्यदनुष्ठितम् ..34..
17.17.m: It is not possible to count the crooked deeds of Viṣṇu; / nevertheless, what was performed by those who were satisfied and delighted is told.

17.17.s:
gaurāṃgī sundarī subhrūḥ pīnonnatapayodharā ..
sukeśā caṃdravadanā karṇāsaktavilocanā..35..
17.17.d:
गौरांगी सुन्दरी सुभ्रूः पीनोन्नतपयोधरा ..
सुकेशा चंद्रवदना कर्णासक्तविलोचना..35..
17.17.m: Fair-limbed, beautiful, with lovely brows and full, high breasts, / with beautiful hair, a moon-like face, and eyes extending to her ears,

17.17.s:
valitrayāṃkitā madhye bālā muṣṭyāpi gṛhyate ..
