sthalāraviṃdacaraṇā lateva bhujabhūṣitā .. 36 ..
17.17.d:
वलित्रयांकिता मध्ये बाला मुष्ट्यापि गृह्यते ..
स्थलारविंदचरणा लतेव भुजभूषिता .. 36 ..
17.17.m: marked with three folds at the waist, a slender maiden graspable even with a fist, / with feet like land-growing lotuses, her arms adorning her like creepers,

17.17.s:
sā sarvābharaṇopetā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutā ..
trailokyamohinī devī saṃjātā'mṛtamanthane .. 37 ..
17.17.d:
सा सर्वाभरणोपेता सर्वलक्षणसंयुता ..
त्रैलोक्यमोहिनी देवी संजाताऽमृतमन्थने .. 37 ..
17.17.m: endowed with all ornaments, possessing all auspicious marks, / the goddess who enchants the three worlds arose at the churning of the nectar.

17.17.s:
amṛtādutthitā pūrvaṃ yasya sā tasya taddhruvam ..
trailokyaṃ vaśagaṃ tasya yasya sā cārulocanā .. 38 ..
17.17.d:
अमृतादुत्थिता पूर्वं यस्य सा तस्य तद्ध्रुवम् ..
त्रैलोक्यं वशगं तस्य यस्य सा चारुलोचना .. 38 ..
17.17.m: She who arose first from the nectar, indeed, belongs to him whose property it is; / the three worlds come under the control of him who possesses that lovely-eyed one.

17.17.s:
tayā saṃmohitāḥ sarve devadānavarākṣasāḥ ..
vimucya manthanaṃ sarve tāṃ grahītuṃ samudyatāḥ .. 39 ..
17.17.d:
तया संमोहिताः सर्वे देवदानवराक्षसाः ..
विमुच्य मन्थनं सर्वे तां ग्रहीतुं समुद्यताः .. 39 ..
17.17.m: Enchanted by her, all the gods, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas / abandoned the churning, and all strove to seize her.

17.17.s:
ekā strī bahavo devā dānavādaityarākṣasāḥ ..
vivādaḥ sumahāñjātaḥ kathamatra bhaviṣyati .. 7.2.17.40 ..
17.17.d:
एका स्त्री बहवो देवा दानवादैत्यराक्षसाः ..
विवादः सुमहाञ्जातः कथमत्र भविष्यति .. 7.2.17.40 ..
17.17.m: There was one woman and many gods, Dānavas, Daityas, and Rākṣasas; / a very great dispute arose: “How will it be resolved here?”

17.17.s:
āgatya viṣṇunā sarve bhuje dhṛtvā nivāritāḥ ..
asyārthe kimaho vādaḥ kriyate bhoḥ parasparam .. 41 ..
17.17.d:
आगत्य विष्णुना सर्वे भुजे धृत्वा निवारिताः ..
अस्यार्थे किमहो वादः क्रियते भोः परस्परम् .. 41 ..
17.17.m: Viṣṇu came, seized everyone by the arm, and restrained them: / “Why, alas, is this argument being held among you for her sake?

17.17.s:
amṛtārthe samārambho mahilārthe vinaśyati ..
saṃketaṃ prathamaṃ kṛtvā viṣṇunā cuṃbitā punaḥ .. 42 ..
17.17.d:
अमृतार्थे समारम्भो महिलार्थे विनश्यति ..
संकेतं प्रथमं कृत्वा विष्णुना चुंबिता पुनः .. 42 ..
17.17.m: An undertaking for the sake of nectar is ruined for the sake of a woman!” / Having first made an agreement, she was kissed again by Viṣṇu.

17.17.s:
divyarūpadharaḥ sragvī vanamālāvibhūṣitaḥ ..
kaustubhoddyotitatanuḥ śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ ..43..
17.17.d:
दिव्यरूपधरः स्रग्वी वनमालाविभूषितः ..
कौस्तुभोद्द्योतिततनुः शंखचक्रगदाधरः ..43..
17.17.m: Wearing a divine form, wearing a garland, adorned with a garland of forest flowers, / his body illuminated by the Kaustubha gem, holding the conch, discus, and mace,

17.17.s:
tasyā haste śubhāṃ mālāṃ dattvā viṣṇuḥ puraḥ sthitaḥ ..
uddhṛtya bāhuṃ sarveṣāṃ babhāṣe vacanaṃ hariḥ .. 44 ..
17.17.d:
तस्या हस्ते शुभां मालां दत्त्वा विष्णुः पुरः स्थितः ..
उद्धृत्य बाहुं सर्वेषां बभाषे वचनं हरिः .. 44 ..
17.17.m: having placed an auspicious garland in her hand, Viṣṇu stood before her; / raising his arm, Hari spoke these words to everyone:

17.17.s:
kurvaṃtu kuṇḍalaṃ sarve tiṣṭhantu svayamāsane ..
vilokya svecchayā lakṣmīrvaramālāṃ prayacchatu .. 45 ..
17.17.d:
कुर्वंतु कुण्डलं सर्वे तिष्ठन्तु स्वयमासने ..
विलोक्य स्वेच्छया लक्ष्मीर्वरमालां प्रयच्छतु .. 45 ..
17.17.m: “Let everyone form a circle and remain seated in their own places; / let Lakṣmī look upon you and bestow the garland of choosing according to her will.

17.17.s:
svayaṃvaravibhedaṃ yaḥ kariṣyatyatilaṃpaṭaḥ ..
sa vadhyaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvaiḥ parastrīlubdhako yathā .. 46 ..
17.17.d:
स्वयंवरविभेदं यः करिष्यत्यतिलंपटः ..
स वध्यः सहितैः सर्वैः परस्त्रीलुब्धको यथा .. 46 ..
17.17.m: Whoever, excessively lustful, causes a disruption to the svayaṃvara, / he must be killed by all together, just like a hunter lusting after another's wife.

17.17.s:
paradārakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ strīvadhyā tasya jāyatām..
anyo'pi yaḥ karotyevamevamastu taducyatām..47..
17.17.d:
परदारकृतं पापं स्त्रीवध्या तस्य जायताम्..
अन्योऽपि यः करोत्येवमेवमस्तु तदुच्यताम्..47..
17.17.m: Let the sin of violating another's wife and the murder of a woman befall him; / let it be proclaimed: ‘So be it!’ for anyone else who acts thus.”

17.17.s:
sādhāraṇaṃ hariṃ jñātvā tathetyuktvā tathā kṛtam..
devadānavadaityānāṃ gaṃdharvoragarakṣasām..
madhye yo'bhimato bhartā sa te satyaṃ bhavediti ..48 ..
17.17.d:
साधारणं हरिं ज्ञात्वा तथेत्युक्त्वा तथा कृतम्..
देवदानवदैत्यानां गंधर्वोरगरक्षसाम्..
मध्ये योऽभिमतो भर्ता स ते सत्यं भवेदिति ..48 ..
17.17.m: Considering Hari impartial, saying “So be it,” they agreed: / “Among gods, Dānavas, Daityas, Gandharvas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, / whoever is favored as a husband, truly he shall be yours.”

17.17.s:
tenāsau mohitā pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭidānena karṣitā ..
ādyaṃ saṃmohanaṃ strīṇāṃ cakre dṛṣṭinirīkṣaṇam..49..
17.17.d:
तेनासौ मोहिता पूर्वं दृष्टिदानेन कर्षिता ..
आद्यं संमोहनं स्त्रीणां चक्रे दृष्टिनिरीक्षणम्..49..
17.17.m: She had already been captivated by him, drawn by the casting of his glance; / looking with a glance was the primary enchantment he cast upon women.

17.17.s:
evameveti tatkarṇe hastaṃ dattvā yaducyate..
dadhāti hṛdi yaṃ nārī kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā .. 7.2.17.50 ..
17.17.d:
एवमेवेति तत्कर्णे हस्तं दत्त्वा यदुच्यते..
दधाति हृदि यं नारी कामबाणप्रपीडिता .. 7.2.17.50 ..
17.17.m: “Just so,” placing a hand to her ear, what was whispered / a woman holds in her heart, afflicted by the arrows of Kāma.

17.17.s:
tameva varayedatra kaścinnāstyeva saṃśayaḥ ..
saṃjāte kalahe pūrvaṃ hariṇā taṃ nivartitum .. 51 ..
17.17.d:
तमेव वरयेदत्र कश्चिन्नास्त्येव संशयः ..
संजाते कलहे पूर्वं हरिणा तं निवर्तितुम् .. 51 ..
17.17.m: She would choose him alone here; there is no doubt at all; / previously, when the quarrel had arisen, Hari had acted to avert it.

17.17.s:
yadā gṛhītā sarvaiḥ sā hariṃ naiva vimuṃcati ..
tvameva bhartā sā''caṣṭe muṃca māṃ vraja dūrataḥ .. 52 ..
17.17.d:
यदा गृहीता सर्वैः सा हरिं नैव विमुंचति ..
त्वमेव भर्ता सा'ऽचष्टे मुंच मां व्रज दूरतः .. 52 ..
17.17.m: When she was seized by all, she did not release Hari at all; / “You alone are my husband,” she said; “Release me, go far away.”

17.17.s:
muktvā dūraṃ tato viṣṇuḥ praviṣṭaḥ suramaṇḍale ..
tadā sarve ca māmuktvā yathāsthānaṃ svayaṃ gatāḥ ..53..
17.17.d:
मुक्त्वा दूरं ततो विष्णुः प्रविष्टः सुरमण्डले ..
तदा सर्वे च मामुक्त्वा यथास्थानं स्वयं गताः ..53..
17.17.m: Having moved away, Viṣṇu then entered among the assembly of gods; / then, having addressed me, they all went to their respective places on their own.

17.17.s:
ācaṣṭa vijayā pūrvaṃ sarvāndevānyathākramam..
sā ca nirīkṣate paścāttaṃ vicārya vimuñcati .. 54 ..
17.17.d:
आचष्ट विजया पूर्वं सर्वान्देवान्यथाक्रमम्..
सा च निरीक्षते पश्चात्तं विचार्य विमुञ्चति .. 54 ..
17.17.m: Vijayā first announced all the gods in proper order; / she looked, and after deliberating upon him, passed him by.

17.17.s:
udāsīnaḥ śivaḥ śāṃto gaurīkāṃtastrilocanaḥ ..
nānyāṃ nirīkṣate nityaṃ dhyānāsaktastrilocanaḥ .. 55 ..
17.17.d:
उदासीनः शिवः शांतो गौरीकांतस्त्रिलोचनः ..
नान्यां निरीक्षते नित्यं ध्यानासक्तस्त्रिलोचनः .. 55 ..
17.17.m: “Śiva is detached, peaceful, the beloved of Gaurī, three-eyed; / he never looks at any other, the three-eyed one ever intent on meditation.”

17.17.s:
pitāmahoyamityuktaṃ yadā sakhyā tadā tayā ..
namaskṛtya gataṃ dūre kṛtvā maunaṃ na paśyati .. 56 ..
17.17.d:
पितामहोयमित्युक्तं यदा सख्या तदा तया ..
नमस्कृत्य गतं दूरे कृत्वा मौनं न पश्यति .. 56 ..
17.17.m: When the female companion said, “This is the Grandfather [Brahmā],” then by her, / having bowed, she went far away, remaining silent and not looking.

17.17.s:
ādityaṃ padmakaṃ muñca dahanaṃ dahanātmakam..
vāti vāto gatā dūre varuṇo me pitā yataḥ .. 57 ..
17.17.d:
आदित्यं पद्मकं मुञ्च दहनं दहनात्मकम्..
वाति वातो गता दूरे वरुणो मे पिता यतः .. 57 ..
17.17.m: “Leave aside the Sun, who brings bloom to lotuses, and Fire, whose nature is burning; / the wind blows,” she went far away, “since Varuṇa is my father.

17.17.s: paulomīvadanāsakto devendro me na rocate .. 58 ..
17.17.d: पौलोमीवदनासक्तो देवेन्द्रो मे न रोचते .. 58 ..
17.17.m: The lord of gods, attached to the face of Paulomī [Śacī], does not please me.”

17.17.s:
vadhabaṃdhakṛtacchedabhedadaṇḍavikarṣa ṇam..
kurvanna kurute saumyaṃ rūpaṃ vaivasvato yamaḥ .. 59 ..
17.17.d:
वधबंधकृतच्छेदभेददण्डविकर्ष णम्..
कुर्वन्न कुरुते सौम्यं रूपं वैवस्वतो यमः .. 59 ..
17.17.m: Inflicting killing, binding, cutting, splitting, punishing, and dragging, / Yama, son of Vivasvat, does not show a gentle form.

17.17.s: devadānavagaṃdharvadaityapannagarākṣasān .. 7.2.17.60 ..
17.17.d: देवदानवगंधर्वदैत्यपन्नगराक्षसान् .. 7.2.17.60 ..
17.17.m: The gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Daityas, serpents, and Rākṣasas—

17.17.s:
dṛṣṭvātyugrāṃstato yāti dṛṣṭo'sau puruṣo ttamaḥ ..
karṇāṃtalocanabhrāṃtavaktraṃ dṛṣṭyāvalokya tam .. 61 ..
17.17.d:
दृष्ट्वात्युग्रांस्ततो याति दृष्टोऽसौ पुरुषो त्तमः ..
कर्णांतलोचनभ्रांतवक्त्रं दृष्ट्यावलोक्य तम् .. 61 ..
17.17.m: seeing them to be exceedingly fierce, she moved on; then that Supreme Person was seen; / having beheld him with her glance, whose face was surrounded by eyes reaching to his ears,

17.17.s:
saubhāgyātiśayākrāṃtaṃ ramyaṃ kāmamanoharam ..
saṃjātapulakodbhedasvedavārikaṇāṃkitam .. .. 62 ..
17.17.d:
सौभाग्यातिशयाक्रांतं रम्यं काममनोहरम् ..
संजातपुलकोद्भेदस्वेदवारिकणांकितम् .. .. 62 ..
17.17.m: pervaded by supreme good fortune, charming, captivating to Kāma, / marked with the bristling of body hairs and droplets of perspiration,

17.17.s:
devadānavadaityendrakrodhadṛṣṭinirīkṣitam ..
ramyaṃ rāmā varaṃ cakre dadau mālāṃ tataḥ svayam..63..
17.17.d:
देवदानवदैत्येन्द्रक्रोधदृष्टिनिरीक्षितम् ..
रम्यं रामा वरं चक्रे ददौ मालां ततः स्वयम्..63..
17.17.m: looked upon with angry glances by the leaders of gods, Dānavas, and Daityas, / the delightful lady chose him as her groom and then personally gave him the garland.

17.17.s:
daityāḥ parasparaṃ procuḥ prekṣya tatsuraceṣṭitam ..
vibhāgaṃ paśya devānāṃ svarge sarve svayaṃ gatāḥ.. 64..
17.17.d:
दैत्याः परस्परं प्रोचुः प्रेक्ष्य तत्सुरचेष्टितम् ..
विभागं पश्य देवानां स्वर्गे सर्वे स्वयं गताः.. 64..
17.17.m: Seeing that conduct of the gods, the Daityas spoke among themselves: / “Look at the division made by the gods! They have all gone to heaven on their own.”

17.17.s:
pātālasya tale yūyaṃ mānavā dharaṇītale..
devāstribhuvane yāṃtu na vayaṃ svargagāminaḥ.. 65..
17.17.d:
पातालस्य तले यूयं मानवा धरणीतले..
देवास्त्रिभुवने यांतु न वयं स्वर्गगामिनः.. 65..
17.17.m: "You [should go] to the bottom of Pātāla; humans [belong] on the surface of the earth; / let the gods go to the triple world; we are not dwellers of heaven."

17.17.s:
mānavāḥ kṣatriyā rājyaṃ kurvaṃtu pṛthivītale..
pātālaṃ tu parityajya dhātrī yadi tu rakṣyate.. 66..
17.17.d:
मानवाः क्षत्रिया राज्यं कुर्वंतु पृथिवीतले..
पातालं तु परित्यज्य धात्री यदि तु रक्ष्यते.. 66..
17.17.m: Let the kṣatriya mortals rule on the surface of the earth. / But if, having abandoned Pātāla, the earth is to be protected,

17.17.s:
daityadānavajaiḥ kaiścidrākṣasaistanna śobhanam..
atha kiṃ bahunoktena rājā tribhuvane baliḥ..67..
17.17.d:
दैत्यदानवजैः कैश्चिद्राक्षसैस्तन्न शोभनम्..
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन राजा त्रिभुवने बलिः..67..
17.17.m: by certain Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas—that is not proper! / But what is the use of much talk? Bali is king in the triple world.

17.17.s:
saṃvibhajyātha ratnāni samaṃ rājyaṃ vidhīyatām..
yāvadevaṃ pragalbhaṃte tāvatpaśyaṃti nāradam .. 68 ..
17.17.d:
संविभज्याथ रत्नानि समं राज्यं विधीयताम्..
यावदेवं प्रगल्भंते तावत्पश्यंति नारदम् .. 68 ..
17.17.m: Having divided the jewels, let the kingdom be ruled equally!" / While they were boasting in this way, they saw Nārada,

17.17.s:
gaganātsamupāyāṃtaṃ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram ..
brahmadaṃḍakarāsaktayuddhapustakadhāriṇam .. 69 ..
17.17.d:
गगनात्समुपायांतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम् ..
ब्रह्मदंडकरासक्तयुद्धपुस्तकधारिणम् .. 69 ..
17.17.m: descending from the sky like a second sun, / carrying a staff of Brahmā in his hand and holding a text on warfare,

17.17.s:
kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ śāṃtaṃ chatravīṇākamaṇḍalūn ..
mauṃjīguṇatrayāsaktagraṃthipravaramekhalam .. 7.2.17.70 ..
17.17.d:
कृष्णाजिनधरं शांतं छत्रवीणाकमण्डलून् ..
मौंजीगुणत्रयासक्तग्रंथिप्रवरमेखलम् .. 7.2.17.70 ..
17.17.m: wearing a black antelope skin, peaceful, with an umbrella, a vīṇā, and a water-pot, / having a fine girdle knotted into three strands of muñja grass,

17.17.s:
brahmarūpadharaṃ śāṃtaṃ divyarudrākṣabhūṣitam ..
gata kalpakṛtagraṃthisūtramālāvalaṃbitam .. 71 ..
17.17.d:
ब्रह्मरूपधरं शांतं दिव्यरुद्राक्षभूषितम् ..
गत कल्पकृतग्रंथिसूत्रमालावलंबितम् .. 71 ..
17.17.m: bearing the form of Brahmā, serene, adorned with celestial rudrākṣa beads, / suspended with a string of sacred cords tied in the past aeon.

17.17.s:
viraṃciharasaṃvādo janmāhaṃkāragarvitaḥ ..
saṃkruddhaiḥ kriyate ko'dya ciṃtātatparamānasam .. .. 72 ..
17.17.d:
विरंचिहरसंवादो जन्माहंकारगर्वितः ..
संक्रुद्धैः क्रियते कोऽद्य चिंतातत्परमानसम् .. .. 72 ..
17.17.m: "A debate between Brahmā and Hara, proud with arrogance of origin, / is now being engaged in by the enraged ones"—his mind was intently absorbed in this thought.

17.17.s:
āyātaṃ nāradaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ samupasthitāḥ ..
prabho prasādaḥ kriyatāmāgaṃtavyaṃ gṛhe mama .. 73 ..
17.17.d:
आयातं नारदं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः समुपस्थिताः ..
प्रभो प्रसादः क्रियतामागंतव्यं गृहे मम .. 73 ..
17.17.m: Seeing that Nārada had arrived, they approached him in astonishment: / "O lord, be gracious! Please come to my house.

17.17.s:
dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ yasya me tvaṃ gṛhāgataḥ ..
ityukto balinā vipro viveśāsuramaṃdire ..
āsanaṃ pādyamarghyaṃ ca dattvā saṃpūjito dvijaḥ .. 74 ..
17.17.d:
धन्योऽहं कृतपुण्योऽहं यस्य मे त्वं गृहागतः ..
इत्युक्तो बलिना विप्रो विवेशासुरमंदिरे ..
आसनं पाद्यमर्घ्यं च दत्त्वा संपूजितो द्विजः .. 74 ..
17.17.m: I am blessed, I have acquired merit, since you have come to my dwelling!" / Thus addressed by Bali, the brahmin entered the residence of the Asura; / having offered a seat, foot-water, and respectful offering, the twice-born was worshipped.

17.17.s:
praviśya sahitāḥ sarve saṃviṣṭā daityadānavāḥ ..
śukreṇa sahito daityo babhāṣe nāradaṃ baliḥ .. 75 ..
17.17.d:
प्रविश्य सहिताः सर्वे संविष्टा दैत्यदानवाः ..
शुक्रेण सहितो दैत्यो बभाषे नारदं बलिः .. 75 ..
17.17.m: Having entered, all the Daityas and Dānavas sat down together. / Along with Śukra, the Daitya Bali addressed Nārada:

17.17.s:
idaṃ rājyamime dārā ime putrā ahaṃ baliḥ ..
brūhi yenātra te kāryaṃ dānaṃ me prathamaṃ vratam .. 76 ..
17.17.d:
इदं राज्यमिमे दारा इमे पुत्रा अहं बलिः ..
ब्रूहि येनात्र ते कार्यं दानं मे प्रथमं व्रतम् .. 76 ..
17.17.m: "Here is my kingdom, here are my wives, here are my sons, and here am I, Bali. / Speak of whatever you have need of here; giving is my foremost vow."

17.17.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
bhaktyā tuṣyaṃti ye viprāste viprā bhūmidevatāḥ ..
na tu ye pūjitāḥ śaktyā punaryācaṃti te'dhamāḥ.. . .. 77 ..
17.17.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
भक्त्या तुष्यंति ये विप्रास्ते विप्रा भूमिदेवताः ..
न तु ये पूजिताः शक्त्या पुनर्याचंति तेऽधमाः.. . .. 77 ..
17.17.m: Nārada said: / "Those brahmins who are pleased with devotion, those brahmins are gods on earth; / but those who, even though worshipped according to one's capacity, beg again—they are the lowest.

17.17.s:
tvayā'haṃ pūjito hṛṣṭo na vittairme prayojanam ..
hṛṣṭo'haṃ tava rājyena yajñairdānairvrataistathā .. 78. ..
devaiḥ kṛtaṃ vipriyaṃ te kiṃcitpaśyāmyahaṃ bale ..
tvayā saṃpūjyamāno'pi devarājo na tuṣyati .. 79 ..
17.17.d:
त्वयाऽहं पूजितो हृष्टो न वित्तैर्मे प्रयोजनम् ..
हृष्टोऽहं तव राज्येन यज्ञैर्दानैर्व्रतैस्तथा .. 78. ..
देवैः कृतं विप्रियं ते किंचित्पश्याम्यहं बले ..
त्वया संपूज्यमानोऽपि देवराजो न तुष्यति .. 79 ..
17.17.m: I have been honored by you and am delighted; I have no need of wealth. / I am pleased by your rule, by your sacrifices, gifts, and vows. / But I see something unpleasant being done against you by the gods, O Bali: / even though honored by you, the king of gods is not satisfied.

17.17.s:
na kṣamaṃti surāḥ sarve tava rājyaṃ dharātale ..
svarge me tāpako jāto devānāṃ tava vigrahe .. .. 7.2.17.80 ..
17.17.d:
न क्षमंति सुराः सर्वे तव राज्यं धरातले ..
स्वर्गे मे तापको जातो देवानां तव विग्रहे .. .. 7.2.17.80 ..
17.17.m: All the gods do not tolerate your dominion on the surface of the earth. / In heaven, grief has arisen for me over the conflict between the gods and you.

17.17.s:
saṃnahya prathamaṃ yāti yaḥ sainyaṃ śatrubhūmiṣu ..
sa kṣatriyo vijayate tasya rājyaṃ ca vardhate ..81..
17.17.d:
संनह्य प्रथमं याति यः सैन्यं शत्रुभूमिषु ..
स क्षत्रियो विजयते तस्य राज्यं च वर्धते ..81..
17.17.m: He who, having armed himself, first marches his army into enemy territory— / that kṣatriya is victorious, and his kingdom increases.

17.17.s:
ucchedastava rājyasya bhaviṣyati śrutaṃ mayā ..
evaṃ jñātvā yathāyuktaṃ tacchīghraṃ tu vidhīyatām .. 82 ..
17.17.d:
उच्छेदस्तव राज्यस्य भविष्यति श्रुतं मया ..
एवं ज्ञात्वा यथायुक्तं तच्छीघ्रं तु विधीयताम् .. 82 ..
17.17.m: The destruction of your kingdom will come to pass; so it has been heard by me. / Knowing this, let whatever is appropriate be done immediately."

17.17.s:
.. baliruvāca .. ..
yairguṇaiḥ kurute rājyaṃ rājā tānvada me vibho ..
dānaṃ pātre pradātavyaṃ mayā tvamapi taṃ vada .. 83 ..
17.17.d:
.. बलिरुवाच .. ..
यैर्गुणैः कुरुते राज्यं राजा तान्वद मे विभो ..
दानं पात्रे प्रदातव्यं मया त्वमपि तं वद .. 83 ..
17.17.m: Bali said: / "O lord, tell me the virtues by which a king rules his kingdom; / I must also bestow gifts upon a worthy recipient—tell me about that as well."

17.17.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
ṣaḍviṃśadguṇasaṃpanno rājā rājyaṃ karoti ca ..
sa rājyaphalamāpnoti śṛṇu tatkathayāmyaham .. 84 ..
17.17.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
षड्विंशद्गुणसंपन्नो राजा राज्यं करोति च ..
स राज्यफलमाप्नोति शृणु तत्कथयाम्यहम् .. 84 ..
17.17.m: Nārada said: / "Endowed with twenty-six virtues, a king rules a kingdom; / he attains the fruit of kingship. Listen, I shall explain it to you.

17.17.s:
careddharmānakaṭuko muṃcetsnehamanāstike ..
anṛśaṃsaścaredarthaṃ caretkāmamanuddhataḥ ..85..
17.17.d:
चरेद्धर्मानकटुको मुंचेत्स्नेहमनास्तिके ..
अनृशंसश्चरेदर्थं चरेत्काममनुद्धतः ..85..
17.17.m: He should practice virtues without bitterness; he should abandon affection for an atheist; / he should pursue wealth without cruelty; he should pursue desire without arrogance.

17.17.s:
priyaṃ brūyādakṛpaṇaḥ śūraḥ syādavikatthanaḥ ..
dātā cā''yāmavarjaḥ syātpragalbhaḥ syādaniṣṭhuraḥ .. 86 ..
17.17.d:
प्रियं ब्रूयादकृपणः शूरः स्यादविकत्थनः ..
दाता चा'ऽयामवर्जः स्यात्प्रगल्भः स्यादनिष्ठुरः .. 86 ..
17.17.m: He should speak pleasantly without being a miser; he should be brave without boasting; / he should be a giver without boundless excess; he should be bold without being harsh.

17.17.s:
saṃdadhīta na cānāryānvigṛhṇīyānna baṃdhubhiḥ ..
nānāptaiścārayeccārānkuryātkāryamapīḍayan ..87..
17.17.d:
संदधीत न चानार्यान्विगृह्णीयान्न बंधुभिः ..
नानाप्तैश्चारयेच्चारान्कुर्यात्कार्यमपीडयन् ..87..
17.17.m: He should not make alliances with the ignoble; he should not quarrel with kinsmen; / he should not employ untrustworthy persons as spies; he should perform his duty without oppressing [others].

17.17.s:
arthānbrūyānna cāpatsu guṇānbrūyānna cātmanaḥ ..
ādadyānna ca sādhubhyo nāsatpuruṣamāśrayet .. 88 ..
17.17.d:
अर्थान्ब्रूयान्न चापत्सु गुणान्ब्रूयान्न चात्मनः ..
आदद्यान्न च साधुभ्यो नासत्पुरुषमाश्रयेत् .. 88 ..
17.17.m: He should not speak of his wealth in times of misfortune; he should not proclaim his own virtues; / he should not seize [property] from the virtuous; he should not rely on a wicked man.

17.17.s:
nāparīkṣya nayeddaṇḍaṃ na ca maṃtraṃ prakāśayet ..
visṛjenna ca lubdhebhyo viśvasennāpakāriṣu .. 89 ..
17.17.d:
नापरीक्ष्य नयेद्दण्डं न च मंत्रं प्रकाशयेत् ..
विसृजेन्न च लुब्धेभ्यो विश्वसेन्नापकारिषु .. 89 ..
17.17.m: He should not inflict punishment without investigation; he should not reveal his counsel; / he should not distribute [wealth] to the greedy; he should not trust harmful persons.

17.17.s:
āptaiḥ suguptadāraḥ syādrakṣyaścānyo ghṛṇī nṛpaḥ ..
striyaṃ seveta nātyarthaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ bhuṃjīta nā'hitam .. 7.2.17.90 ..
17.17.d:
आप्तैः सुगुप्तदारः स्याद्रक्ष्यश्चान्यो घृणी नृपः ..
स्त्रियं सेवेत नात्यर्थं मृष्टं भुंजीत नाऽहितम् .. 7.2.17.90 ..
17.17.m: His wives should be well protected by trusted guards; he should protect others; a king should be compassionate; / he should not indulge excessively in women; he should eat wholesome food, not unwholesome.

17.17.s:
asteyaḥ pūjayenmānyānguruṃ sevedamāyayā ..
arcyo devo na dambhena śriyamicchedakutsitām .. 91 ..
17.17.d:
अस्तेयः पूजयेन्मान्यान्गुरुं सेवेदमायया ..
अर्च्यो देवो न दम्भेन श्रियमिच्छेदकुत्सिताम् .. 91 ..
17.17.m: He should not steal; he should honor the venerable; he should serve his guru without deceit; / a deity should be worshipped without hypocrisy; he should desire wealth that is not blameworthy.

17.17.s:
seveta praṇayaṃ kṛtvā dakṣaḥ syādatha kālavit ..
sāṃtvavākyaṃ sadā vācyamanugṛhṇanna cākṣipet.. 92 ..
17.17.d:
सेवेत प्रणयं कृत्वा दक्षः स्यादथ कालवित् ..
सांत्ववाक्यं सदा वाच्यमनुगृह्णन्न चाक्षिपेत्.. 92 ..
17.17.m: He should serve with genuine affection; he should be skillful and know the proper time; / soothing speech should always be spoken; while showing favor, he should not rebuke.

17.17.s:
praharenna ca viprāya hatvā śatrūnna śeṣayet ..
krodhaṃ kuryānna cākasmānmṛduḥ syānnāpakāriṣu .. 93 ..
17.17.d:
प्रहरेन्न च विप्राय हत्वा शत्रून्न शेषयेत् ..
क्रोधं कुर्यान्न चाकस्मान्मृदुः स्यान्नापकारिषु .. 93 ..
17.17.m: He should not strike a brahmin; having defeated his enemies, he should leave no remnant; / he should not show anger without cause; he should not be mild toward wrongdoers.

17.17.s:
evaṃ rājye ciraṃ stheyaṃ yadi śreya ihecchasi ..
tapaḥsvādhyāyadānāni tīrthayātrā''śramāṇi ca .. 94 ..
17.17.d:
एवं राज्ये चिरं स्थेयं यदि श्रेय इहेच्छसि ..
तपःस्वाध्यायदानानि तीर्थयात्रा'ऽश्रमाणि च .. 94 ..
17.17.m: Thus one should abide in kingship for a long time, if you desire welfare in this world. / Austerities, recitation of sacred texts, gifts, pilgrimages to sacred fords, and life in hermitages—

17.17.s:
yogenātmaprabodhasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm ..
tvayā saṃsāravairāgyaṃ karttavyaṃ viprapūjanam ..95..
17.17.d:
योगेनात्मप्रबोधस्य कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम् ..
त्वया संसारवैराग्यं कर्त्तव्यं विप्रपूजनम् ..95..
17.17.m: do not equal even a sixteenth part of self-realization through yoga. / You should practice detachment from worldly existence and the honoring of brahmins.

17.17.s:
yaṣṭavyaṃ vividhairyajñairdhyeyo nārāyaṇo hariḥ ..
prasaṃgena samāyāto yāsye raivatake girau .. 96 ..
17.17.d:
यष्टव्यं विविधैर्यज्ञैर्ध्येयो नारायणो हरिः ..
प्रसंगेन समायातो यास्ये रैवतके गिरौ .. 96 ..
17.17.m: Worship should be offered through diverse sacrifices; Hari, Nārāyaṇa, is to be meditated upon. / I have arrived here incidentally, and I shall proceed to Mount Raivataka.

17.17.s:
tatrāste bhagavānviṣṇurnadī trailokyapāvanī ..
tatrāste ca śivāvṛkṣo bahupuṣpaphalānvitaḥ ..
tatra gatvā kariṣyāmi vrataṃ tadviṣṇuvallabham .. 97 ..
17.17.d:
तत्रास्ते भगवान्विष्णुर्नदी त्रैलोक्यपावनी ..
तत्रास्ते च शिवावृक्षो बहुपुष्पफलान्वितः ..
तत्र गत्वा करिष्यामि व्रतं तद्विष्णुवल्लभम् .. 97 ..
17.17.m: There abides Lord Viṣṇu and the river that purifies the three worlds; / and there stands the Śivā tree, rich with abundant flowers and fruits. / Going there, I shall observe that vow dear to Viṣṇu."

17.17.s:
.. baliruvāca .. ..
ko'yaṃ raivatakonāma vrataṃ kiṃ viṣṇuvallabham ..
śivāvṛkṣāstu ke proktāstatkathaṃ kathayasva me .. 98 .. ..
17.17.d:
.. बलिरुवाच .. ..
कोऽयं रैवतकोनाम व्रतं किं विष्णुवल्लभम् ..
शिवावृक्षास्तु के प्रोक्तास्तत्कथं कथयस्व मे .. 98 .. ..
17.17.m: Bali said: / "What is this [mountain] named Raivataka? What is the vow dear to Viṣṇu? / And what are the Śivā trees that are spoken of? Tell me that in detail."

17.17.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
purā yugādau daityendra sapakṣāḥ parvatāḥ kṛtāḥ ..
saṃciṃtya brahmaṇā paścādacalāste kṛtāḥ punaḥ .. 99 ..
17.17.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
पुरा युगादौ दैत्येन्द्र सपक्षाः पर्वताः कृताः ..
संचिंत्य ब्रह्मणा पश्चादचलास्ते कृताः पुनः .. 99 ..
17.17.m: Nārada said: / "Formerly, at the beginning of the yuga, O lord of Daityas, mountains were made with wings; / later, having deliberated, Brahmā made them immobile again.

17.17.s:
utpataṃti mahākāyā nipataṃti yadṛcchayā ..
merumaṃdarakailāsā vacasā saṃsthitāḥ sthirāḥ .. 7.2.17.100 ..
17.17.d:
उत्पतंति महाकाया निपतंति यदृच्छया ..
मेरुमंदरकैलासा वचसा संस्थिताः स्थिराः .. 7.2.17.100 ..
17.17.m: Huge in body, they would fly up and descend at will. / Meru, Mandara, and Kailāsa remained fixed by his command alone.

17.17.s:
vāritā na sthitā ye tu ta iṃdreṇa sthirīkṛtāḥ ..
merordakṣiṇa śṛṃge tu kumudeti sa parvataḥ .. 101 ..
17.17.d:
वारिता न स्थिता ये तु त इंद्रेण स्थिरीकृताः ..
मेरोर्दक्षिण शृंगे तु कुमुदेति स पर्वतः .. 101 ..
17.17.m: Those that were checked but would not remain still were rendered stationary by Indra. / On the southern peak of Meru is that mountain called Kumuda,

17.17.s:
divyaḥ sapakṣaḥ sauvarṇo divyavṛkṣaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ ..
tasyopari purī divyā vaiṣṇavī viṣṇunā kṛtā .. 102 ..
17.17.d:
दिव्यः सपक्षः सौवर्णो दिव्यवृक्षैः समावृतः ..
तस्योपरि पुरी दिव्या वैष्णवी विष्णुना कृता .. 102 ..
17.17.m: divine, winged, golden, covered with heavenly trees. / Upon it a divine city of Viṣṇu was built by Viṣṇu.

17.17.s:
tasyā madhye gṛhaṃ divyaṃ yasmillam̐kṣmīḥ sadā sthitā ..
meroḥ śṛṃge purī ramyā gṛhaṃ tatra manoramam .. 103 ..
17.17.d:
तस्या मध्ये गृहं दिव्यं यस्मिल्लम्̐क्ष्मीः सदा स्थिता ..
मेरोः शृंगे पुरी रम्या गृहं तत्र मनोरमम् .. 103 ..
17.17.m: In the middle of it is a divine mansion in which Lakṣmī is ever present. / On the peak of Meru is a delightful city, and there is an enchanting palace;

17.17.s:
tatrāste sa bhavo devo bhavānī yatra saṃsthitā ..
sabhā māheśvarī ramyā sauvarṇī ratnamaṃḍitā .. 104 ..
17.17.d:
तत्रास्ते स भवो देवो भवानी यत्र संस्थिता ..
सभा माहेश्वरी रम्या सौवर्णी रत्नमंडिता .. 104 ..
17.17.m: there abides the god Bhava, where Bhavānī is seated. / There is the lovely assembly hall of Maheśvara, made of gold and adorned with jewels.

17.17.s:
tatrāste bhagavānviṣṇurdevairbrahmādibhirvṛtaḥ ..
tasyāṃ viṣṇuḥ sadā yāti devaṃ draṣṭuṃ maheśvaram .. 105 ..
17.17.d:
तत्रास्ते भगवान्विष्णुर्देवैर्ब्रह्मादिभिर्वृतः ..
तस्यां विष्णुः सदा याति देवं द्रष्टुं महेश्वरम् .. 105 ..
17.17.m: There abides Lord Viṣṇu, surrounded by the gods led by Brahmā; / Viṣṇu always goes to that assembly to see the god Maheśvara.

17.17.s:
sauvarṇaiḥ kumudairyasmādasau sarvatra maṃḍitaḥ ..
kumudeti kṛtaṃ nāma devaistatra samāgataiḥ .. 106 ..
17.17.d:
सौवर्णैः कुमुदैर्यस्मादसौ सर्वत्र मंडितः ..
कुमुदेति कृतं नाम देवैस्तत्र समागतैः .. 106 ..
17.17.m: Because it was adorned everywhere with golden water-lilies, / the gods who gathered there gave it the name Kumuda.

17.17.s:
ekadā bhagavānrudro girau tasminsamāgataḥ ..
draṣṭuṃ tacchikhare ramye tāṃ purīṃ viṣṇupālitām .. 107 ..
17.17.d:
एकदा भगवान्रुद्रो गिरौ तस्मिन्समागतः ..
द्रष्टुं तच्छिखरे रम्ये तां पुरीं विष्णुपालिताम् .. 107 ..
17.17.m: Once the blessed Rudra came to that mountain / to see that city protected by Viṣṇu on its delightful peak.

17.17.s:
gṛhāgataṃ haraṃ dṛṣṭvā hariṇā sa tu pūjitaḥ ..
lakṣmyā saṃpūjitā gaurī harṣitā tatra saṃsthitā .. 108 ..
17.17.d:
गृहागतं हरं दृष्ट्वा हरिणा स तु पूजितः ..
लक्ष्म्या संपूजिता गौरी हर्षिता तत्र संस्थिता .. 108 ..
17.17.m: Seeing Hara arrived at his abode, he was worshipped by Hari; / and Gaurī, worshipped by Lakṣmī, remained there delighted.

17.17.s:
ekāsanopaviṣṭau tau maṃtrayaṃtau parasparam ..
hareṇa kāraṇaṃ jñātvā tatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ hareḥ .. 109 ..
17.17.d:
एकासनोपविष्टौ तौ मंत्रयंतौ परस्परम् ..
हरेण कारणं ज्ञात्वा तत्सर्वं कथितं हरेः .. 109 ..
17.17.m: The two seated upon a single throne deliberated with each other; / knowing the reason through Hara, everything was told to Hari:

17.17.s:
tvayeyaṃ nagarī kāryā maṃdare parvatottame ..
praṣṭavyaḥ kāraṇaṃ nāhamavaśyaṃ tadbhaviṣyati .. 7.2.17.110 ..
17.17.d:
त्वयेयं नगरी कार्या मंदरे पर्वतोत्तमे ..
प्रष्टव्यः कारणं नाहमवश्यं तद्भविष्यति .. 7.2.17.110 ..
17.17.m: “This city must be made by you on Mandara, the excellent mountain. / I should not be asked the reason; it will certainly come to pass.

17.17.s:
hara eva vijānāti kāraṇaṃ katamo'pi na ..
evaṃ tatheti tau proktvā saṃsthitau parvato'pi saḥ .. 111 ..
17.17.d:
हर एव विजानाति कारणं कतमोऽपि न ..
एवं तथेति तौ प्रोक्त्वा संस्थितौ पर्वतोऽपि सः .. 111 ..
17.17.m: Hara alone knows the reason, and no one else at all.” / Having said, “So be it,” they remained; that mountain too [remained].

17.17.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃgataṃ rudraṃ kumudaḥ svayamāyayau ..
dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ yasya me gṛhamāgatau .. 112 ..
17.17.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा संगतं रुद्रं कुमुदः स्वयमाययौ ..
धन्योऽहं कृतपुण्योऽहं यस्य मे गृहमागतौ .. 112 ..
17.17.m: Seeing that Rudra had arrived, Kumuda himself approached: / “Blessed am I, my merit is accomplished, since the two of you have come to my home.”

17.17.s:
dvābhyāmukto girivaro dadāva kiṃ varaṃ tava ..
ityuktaḥ parvatastābhyāṃ varaṃ vavre sa mūḍhadhīḥ .. 113 ..
17.17.d:
द्वाभ्यामुक्तो गिरिवरो ददाव किं वरं तव ..
इत्युक्तः पर्वतस्ताभ्यां वरं वव्रे स मूढधीः .. 113 ..
17.17.m: Addressed by both: “O best of mountains, what boon shall we grant you?” / Being addressed thus by them, he, dull-witted, chose a boon.

17.17.s:
bhaviṣyatkāryahetutvādbhaviṣyati na tadvṛthā ..
yatrāhaṃ tatra vastavyaṃ bhavadbhyāmastu me varaḥ .. 114 ..
17.17.d:
भविष्यत्कार्यहेतुत्वाद्भविष्यति न तद्वृथा ..
यत्राहं तत्र वस्तव्यं भवद्भ्यामस्तु मे वरः .. 114 ..
17.17.m: Because it is the cause of future events, it will not be in vain: / “Wherever I am, there the two of you must dwell; let this be my boon.

17.17.s:
matsannidhau samāgatya sthātavyaṃ brahmavāsaram ..
tathetyuktvā sapatnīkau gatau hariharāvubhau .. 116 ..
pañcamo yo manuḥ pūrvaṃ raivato nāma viśrutaḥ ..
tasyotpattau tu yadvṛttaṃ kumudāgre śṛṇuṣva tat .. 116 ..
17.17.d:
मत्सन्निधौ समागत्य स्थातव्यं ब्रह्मवासरम् ..
तथेत्युक्त्वा सपत्नीकौ गतौ हरिहरावुभौ .. 116 ..
पञ्चमो यो मनुः पूर्वं रैवतो नाम विश्रुतः ..
तस्योत्पत्तौ तु यद्वृत्तं कुमुदाग्रे शृणुष्व तत् .. 116 ..
17.17.m:
Coming into my presence, you must remain for a day of Brahmā.” / Saying, “So be it,” both Hari and Hara, with their consorts, departed.
The fifth Manu, who was formerly renowned by the name Raivata— / hear that which occurred before Kumuda at his birth.

17.17.s:
ṛṣirāsīnmahābhāga ṛtavāgiti viśrutaḥ ..
tasyāputrasya putro'bhūdrevatyante mahātmanaḥ .. 117 ..
17.17.d:
ऋषिरासीन्महाभाग ऋतवागिति विश्रुतः ..
तस्यापुत्रस्य पुत्रोऽभूद्रेवत्यन्ते महात्मनः .. 117 ..
17.17.m: There was an illustrious seer renowned as Ṛtavāc; / to that childless, great-souled one, a son was born at the end of Revatī.

17.17.s:
sa tasya vidhivaccakre jātakarmādikāḥ kriyāḥ ..
tathopanayanādyāśca sa cāśīlo'bhavannṛpa .. 118 ..
17.17.d:
स तस्य विधिवच्चक्रे जातकर्मादिकाः क्रियाः ..
तथोपनयनाद्याश्च स चाशीलोऽभवन्नृप .. 118 ..
17.17.m: He performed for him according to rule the birth-rites and other ceremonies, / as well as the sacred thread ceremony and the like; but he turned out ill-behaved, O king.

17.17.s:
yataḥ prabhṛti jāto'sau tataḥ prabhṛtyasāvṛṣiḥ ..
dīrgharogaparāmarśamavāpātīva durddharam .. 119 ...
17.17.d:
यतः प्रभृति जातोऽसौ ततः प्रभृत्यसावृषिः ..
दीर्घरोगपरामर्शमवापातीव दुर्द्धरम् .. 119 ...
17.17.m: From the time he was born, from that time forth, that seer / suffered the affliction of a chronic illness, exceedingly hard to bear.

17.17.s:
mātā cāsya parāmārtiṃ kuṣṭharogābhipīḍitā ..
jagāma cintāṃ sa ṛṣiḥ kimetaditi duḥkhitaḥ .. 7.2.17.120 ..
17.17.d:
माता चास्य परामार्तिं कुष्ठरोगाभिपीडिता ..
जगाम चिन्तां स ऋषिः किमेतदिति दुःखितः .. 7.2.17.120 ..
17.17.m: And his mother, afflicted with leprosy, came to supreme distress. / The seer, grieving, fell into anxious thought: “What is this?”

17.17.s:
mūrkhastu maṃdadhīḥ putro duḥkhaṃ janayate pituḥ ..
amārgago viśeṣeṇa duḥkhādduḥkhataraṃ hi tat .. 121 ..
17.17.d:
मूर्खस्तु मंदधीः पुत्रो दुःखं जनयते पितुः ..
अमार्गगो विशेषेण दुःखाद्दुःखतरं हि तत् .. 121 ..
17.17.m: “A foolish, dull-witted son causes sorrow to his father; / one who walks the wrong path especially—that is indeed worse than grief.

17.17.s:
aputratā manuṣyāṇāṃ śreyase na kuputratā ..
suhṛdāṃ nopakārāya pitṝṇāṃ nāpi tṛptaye .. 122 ..
17.17.d:
अपुत्रता मनुष्याणां श्रेयसे न कुपुत्रता ..
सुहृदां नोपकाराय पितॄणां नापि तृप्तये .. 122 ..
17.17.m: Childlessness is better for men, not a wicked son; / [he is] of no benefit to friends, nor for the satisfaction of the ancestors.

17.17.s:
suputro hṛdaye'bhyeti mātāpitrordinedine ..
pitrorduḥkhāya dhigjanma tasya duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ .. 123 ..
17.17.d:
सुपुत्रो हृदयेऽभ्येति मातापित्रोर्दिनेदिने ..
पित्रोर्दुःखाय धिग्जन्म तस्य दुष्कृतकर्मणः .. 123 ..
17.17.m: A good son enters day after day into the heart of his parents; / cursed is the birth of that evil-doer who causes grief to his parents!

17.17.s:
dhanyāste tanayā ye syuḥ savarlokābhisaṃmatāḥ ..
paropakāriṇaḥ śāṃtāḥ sādhukarmaṇyanuvratāḥ .. 124 ..
17.17.d:
धन्यास्ते तनया ये स्युः सवर्लोकाभिसंमताः ..
परोपकारिणः शांताः साधुकर्मण्यनुव्रताः .. 124 ..
17.17.m: Blessed are those sons who are esteemed by all the world, / benevolent to others, peaceful, devoted to virtuous deeds.

17.17.s:
anirvṛtaṃ nirānaṃdaṃ duḥkhaśokapariplutam ..
narakāya na svargāya kuputratvaṃ hi janminaḥ .. 125 ..
17.17.d:
अनिर्वृतं निरानंदं दुःखशोकपरिप्लुतम् ..
नरकाय न स्वर्गाय कुपुत्रत्वं हि जन्मिनः .. 125 ..
17.17.m: Discontented, joyless, overwhelmed with sorrow and grief, / the state of having a wicked son leads the living being to hell, not to heaven.

17.17.s:
karoti suhṛdāṃ dainyamahitānāṃ tathā mudam ..
akāle tu jarāṃ pitroḥ kuputraḥ kurute kila .. 126 ..
17.17.d:
करोति सुहृदां दैन्यमहितानां तथा मुदम् ..
अकाले तु जरां पित्रोः कुपुत्रः कुरुते किल .. 126 ..
17.17.m: It causes misery to friends and likewise delight to enemies; / indeed, a wicked son brings premature old age upon his parents.”

17.17.s:
.. nārada uvāca ..
evaṃ so'tyantaduṣṭasya putrasya caritairmuniḥ ..
dahyamānamanovṛttirvṛddhagargamapṛcchata .. 127 ..
17.17.d:
.. नारद उवाच ..
एवं सोऽत्यन्तदुष्टस्य पुत्रस्य चरितैर्मुनिः ..
दह्यमानमनोवृत्तिर्वृद्धगर्गमपृच्छत .. 127 ..
17.17.m: Nārada said: / Thus that sage, his mind burning with anguish / over the deeds of that exceedingly wicked son, questioned the elder Garga.

17.17.s:
.. ṛtavāguvāca .. ..
suvratena purā vedā adhītā vidhinā mayā ..
samāpya vidyā vidhavatkṛto dāraparigrahaḥ .. 128 ..
17.17.d:
.. ऋतवागुवाच .. ..
सुव्रतेन पुरा वेदा अधीता विधिना मया ..
समाप्य विद्या विधवत्कृतो दारपरिग्रहः .. 128 ..
17.17.m: Ṛtavāc said: / “Formerly, maintaining good vows, the Vedas were studied by me according to rule; / having completed my studies, I took a wife according to injunction.

17.17.s:
sadāreṇa hi yāḥ kāryāḥ śrautasmārttādikāḥ kriyāḥ ..
tāḥ kṛtāśca vidhānena kāmaṃ samanurudhya ca .. 129 ..
17.17.d:
सदारेण हि याः कार्याः श्रौतस्मार्त्तादिकाः क्रियाः ..
ताः कृताश्च विधानेन कामं समनुरुध्य च .. 129 ..
17.17.m: Whatever rites, based on Śruti and Smṛti, are to be performed with a wife, / those were performed according to ordinance and in accordance with desire.

17.17.s:
putrārthaṃ janitaścāyaṃ puṃnāmno vicyutau mune ..
so'yaṃ kimātmadoṣeṇa māturdoṣeṇa kiṃ mama ..
asmadduḥkhāvaho jāto dauḥśīlyādvada kovida .. 7.2.17.130 ..
17.17.d:
पुत्रार्थं जनितश्चायं पुंनाम्नो विच्युतौ मुने ..
सोऽयं किमात्मदोषेण मातुर्दोषेण किं मम ..
अस्मद्दुःखावहो जातो दौःशील्याद्वद कोविद .. 7.2.17.130 ..
17.17.m: And for the sake of a son he was begotten to save me from the hell named Put, O sage; / has he been born bringing sorrow to us through wicked conduct by his own fault, or by his mother's fault, or by mine? Tell me, O learned one!”

17.17.s:
.. garga uvāca .. ..
revatyante muniśreṣṭha jāto'yaṃ tanayastava ..
tena duḥkhāya te duṣṭe kāle yasmādajāyata .. 131 ..
17.17.d:
.. गर्ग उवाच .. ..
रेवत्यन्ते मुनिश्रेष्ठ जातोऽयं तनयस्तव ..
तेन दुःखाय ते दुष्टे काले यस्मादजायत .. 131 ..
17.17.m: Garga said: / “O best of sages, this son of yours was born at the end of Revatī; / therefore he is for your sorrow, because he was born at an evil time.

17.17.s:
tavāpacāro naivāsya māturnāpi kulasya ca ..
anyaddauḥśīlyahetutvaṃ revatyaṃta upāgatam .. 132 ..
17.17.d:
तवापचारो नैवास्य मातुर्नापि कुलस्य च ..
अन्यद्दौःशील्यहेतुत्वं रेवत्यंत उपागतम् .. 132 ..
17.17.m: There is no wrongdoing on your part, nor on the mother's, nor on the family's; / the cause of his ill behaviour is something else, arrived at the end of Revatī.

17.17.s:
revatī aśvinormadhyamāśleṣāmaghayostathā ..
jyeṣṭhāmūlarkṣayoḥ proktaṃ gaṃḍāṃtaṃ tu bhayāvaham .. 133 ..
17.17.d:
रेवती अश्विनोर्मध्यमाश्लेषामघयोस्तथा ..
ज्येष्ठामूलर्क्षयोः प्रोक्तं गंडांतं तु भयावहम् .. 133 ..
17.17.m: The junction between Revatī and Aśvinī, and likewise between Āśleṣā and Maghā, / and between Jyeṣṭhā and Mūla, is declared to be the dreadful Gaṇḍānta.

17.17.s:
gaṃḍatraye tu ye jātā naranārīturaṃgamāḥ ..
tiṣṭhaṃti na ciraṃ gehe tiṣṭhanto'pi bhayaṃkarāḥ ..
evamukto'tha gargeṇa cukrodhātīva kopanaḥ .. 134 ..
17.17.d:
गंडत्रये तु ये जाता नरनारीतुरंगमाः ..
तिष्ठंति न चिरं गेहे तिष्ठन्तोऽपि भयंकराः ..
एवमुक्तोऽथ गर्गेण चुक्रोधातीव कोपनः .. 134 ..
17.17.m: Whatever men, women, or horses are born in the three Gaṇḍas / do not stay long in the house, and even while staying, they are terrifying.” / Addressed thus by Garga, he, very prone to anger, became exceedingly enraged.

17.17.s:
.. ṛtavāguvāca .. ..
yasmānmamaika putrasya revatyante samudbhavaḥ .. 135 ..
17.17.d:
.. ऋतवागुवाच .. ..
यस्मान्ममैक पुत्रस्य रेवत्यन्ते समुद्भवः .. 135 ..
17.17.m: Ṛtavāc said: / “Because my only son was born at the end of Revatī,

17.17.s:
revatī kiṃ na jānāti māṃ vipraḥ śāpayiṣyati ..
jājvalyamānā gaganāttasmātpatatu revatī .. 136 .. ..
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
tenaivaṃ vyāhṛte vākye revatyṛkṣaṃ papāta ha ..
17.17.d:
रेवती किं न जानाति मां विप्रः शापयिष्यति ..
जाज्वल्यमाना गगनात्तस्मात्पततु रेवती .. 136 .. ..
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
तेनैवं व्याहृते वाक्ये रेवत्यृक्षं पपात ह ..
17.17.m:
did Revatī not know: ‘A brahmin will curse me’? / Therefore, let Revatī fall from the sky, blazing furiously!”
Nārada said: / When that word was uttered by him, the asterism Revatī fell indeed,

17.17.s: paśyataḥ sarvalokasya vismayāviṣṭacetasaḥ .. 137 ..
17.17.d: पश्यतः सर्वलोकस्य विस्मयाविष्टचेतसः .. 137 ..
17.17.m: while all the world watched, their minds filled with wonder.

17.17.s:
īśvarecchāprabhāvena patitā girimūrddhani ..
revatyṛkṣaṃ nipatitaṃ kumudādrau samantataḥ .. 138 ..
17.17.d:
ईश्वरेच्छाप्रभावेन पतिता गिरिमूर्द्धनि ..
रेवत्यृक्षं निपतितं कुमुदाद्रौ समन्ततः .. 138 ..
17.17.m: By the power of the Lord's will, it fell upon the mountain's peak; / the asterism Revatī fell down all around upon Mount Kumuda.

17.17.s:
surāṣṭradeśe sa prāptaḥ patito bhūtale śubhe ..
himācalasya putro ya ujjayaṃto girirmahān.. 139 ..
17.17.d:
सुराष्ट्रदेशे स प्राप्तः पतितो भूतले शुभे ..
हिमाचलस्य पुत्रो य उज्जयंतो गिरिर्महान्.. 139 ..
17.17.m: It reached the country of Surāṣṭra and fell on the auspicious earth. / The great mountain Ujjayanta, the son of the Himālaya,

17.17.s:
kumudena samaṃ maitrī kṛtā pūrvaṃ parasparam ..
yatra tvaṃ sthāsyase sthātā tatrāhamapi niścitam .. 7.2.17.140 ..
17.17.d:
कुमुदेन समं मैत्री कृता पूर्वं परस्परम् ..
यत्र त्वं स्थास्यसे स्थाता तत्राहमपि निश्चितम् .. 7.2.17.140 ..
17.17.m: had previously made mutual friendship with Kumuda: / “Wherever you will stay, there I too shall certainly stay.”

17.17.s:
iti kṛtvā gṛhītvātha gaṃgāvāri sayāmunam ..
sārasvataṃ tathā puṇyaṃ siṃcituṃ taṃ samāgataḥ .. 141 ..
17.17.d:
इति कृत्वा गृहीत्वाथ गंगावारि सयामुनम् ..
सारस्वतं तथा पुण्यं सिंचितुं तं समागतः .. 141 ..
17.17.m: Having done this, taking water from the Gaṅgā along with the Yamunā / and the holy belonging to Sarasvatī, he came to sprinkle it.

17.17.s:
āhūtasaṃplavaṃ yāvatsaṃsthitau tau parasparam ..
kumudādriśca tatpātātkhyāto raivatako'bhavat .. 142 ..
17.17.d:
आहूतसंप्लवं यावत्संस्थितौ तौ परस्परम् ..
कुमुदाद्रिश्च तत्पातात्ख्यातो रैवतकोऽभवत् .. 142 ..
17.17.m: The two stayed together until the universal deluge was summoned; / and from that fall, Mount Kumuda became renowned as Raivataka.

17.17.s:
atīva ramyaḥ sarvasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate ..
kumudādriśca sauvarṇo revatīcyavanātpunaḥ .. 143 ..
17.17.d:
अतीव रम्यः सर्वस्यां पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते ..
कुमुदाद्रिश्च सौवर्णो रेवतीच्यवनात्पुनः .. 143 ..
17.17.m: It is exceedingly delightful on the whole earth, O lord of the earth; / and Mount Kumuda, golden, because of the falling of Revatī,

17.17.s:
paṃkajābhaḥ sa bāhyena jāto varṇena bhūpate ..
meruvarṇaḥ sa madhye tu sauvarṇaḥ parvatottamaḥ .. 144 ..
17.17.d:
पंकजाभः स बाह्येन जातो वर्णेन भूपते ..
मेरुवर्णः स मध्ये तु सौवर्णः पर्वतोत्तमः .. 144 ..
17.17.m: became lotus-hued on its exterior, O king; / but in its middle, that best of mountains was Meru-hued, golden.

17.17.s:
tataḥ sañjanayāmāsa kanyāṃ raivatako giriḥ ..
revatīkāṃti saṃbhūtāṃ revatīsadṛśānanām.. 145 ..
17.17.d:
ततः सञ्जनयामास कन्यां रैवतको गिरिः ..
रेवतीकांति संभूतां रेवतीसदृशाननाम्.. 145 ..
17.17.m: Then Mount Raivataka produced a maiden / born from the splendour of Revatī, whose face was like Revatī.

17.17.s:
pramuco nāma rājarṣistena dṛṣṭā varāṃganā ..
pitṛvadrevatīnāma kṛtaṃ tasyā nṛpottama .. 146 ..
17.17.d:
प्रमुचो नाम राजर्षिस्तेन दृष्टा वरांगना ..
पितृवद्रेवतीनाम कृतं तस्या नृपोत्तम .. 146 ..
17.17.m: An excellent woman was seen by the royal sage named Pramuca; / like a father, the name Revatī was given to her, O best of kings.

17.17.s:
revatīti ca vikhyātā sā sarvatra varāṃganā ..
sarvatejomayaṃ sthānaṃ sarvatīrthajalāśrayam .. 147 ..
17.17.d:
रेवतीति च विख्याता सा सर्वत्र वरांगना ..
सर्वतेजोमयं स्थानं सर्वतीर्थजलाश्रयम् .. 147 ..
17.17.m: And that excellent woman became renowned everywhere as Revatī; / [that mountain is] a place composed of all splendour, the resort of the waters of all sacred fords.

17.17.s:
gaṃgājalapravāhaiśca saṃyuktaṃ yāmunaistathā ..
sthitaṃ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ tatra garteṣu tattrayam .. 148 ..
17.17.d:
गंगाजलप्रवाहैश्च संयुक्तं यामुनैस्तथा ..
स्थितं सारस्वतं तोयं तत्र गर्तेषु तत्त्रयम् .. 148 ..
17.17.m: joined with streams of Gaṅgā water as well as those of the Yamunā; / the water belonging to Sarasvatī stayed there—those three [waters] within the pits.

17.17.s:
vikhyātaṃ revatīkuṃḍaṃ yatra jātā ca revatī ..
smaraṇāddarśanātsnānātsarvapāpakṣayo bhavet .. 149 ..
17.17.d:
विख्यातं रेवतीकुंडं यत्र जाता च रेवती ..
स्मरणाद्दर्शनात्स्नानात्सर्वपापक्षयो भवेत् .. 149 ..
17.17.m: It is known as Revatīkuṇḍa, where Revatī was born. / By remembering it, by seeing it, and by ritual ablution, destruction of all sins takes place.

17.17.s:
sā bālā varddhitā tena pramuṃcena mahātmanā ..
yauvanaṃ tu tayā prāptaṃ tasminraivatake girau .. 7.2.17.150 ..
17.17.d:
सा बाला वर्द्धिता तेन प्रमुंचेन महात्मना ..
यौवनं तु तया प्राप्तं तस्मिन्रैवतके गिरौ .. 7.2.17.150 ..
17.17.m: That girl was brought up by that noble Pramuca; / and she attained youth on that Raivataka mountain.

17.17.s:
tāṃ tu yauvanasaṃpannāṃ dṛṣṭvā'tha pramuco muni ..
ekāṃte cintayāmāsa ko'syā bhartā bhaviṣyati .. 151 ..
17.17.d:
तां तु यौवनसंपन्नां दृष्ट्वाऽथ प्रमुचो मुनि ..
एकांते चिन्तयामास कोऽस्या भर्ता भविष्यति .. 151 ..
17.17.m: Then, seeing her endowed with youth, the sage Pramuca / pondered in solitude: "Who will be her husband?"

17.17.s:
hūtvāhūtvā sa papraccha guruṃ vahniṃ dvijottamaḥ ..
prasādaṃ kuru me brūhi ko'syā bhartā bhaviṣyati .. 152 ..
17.17.d:
हूत्वाहूत्वा स पप्रच्छ गुरुं वह्निं द्विजोत्तमः ..
प्रसादं कुरु मे ब्रूहि कोऽस्या भर्ता भविष्यति .. 152 ..
17.17.m: Offering oblations again and again, that best of brahmins asked his preceptor, the fire: / "Grant me favor! Tell me, who will be her husband?

17.17.s:
anyo'syāḥ sadṛśaḥ ko'pi vaṃśe nāsti karomi kim ..
vahnikuṇḍātsamutthāya proktavānhavyavāhanaḥ .. 153 ..
17.17.d:
अन्योऽस्याः सदृशः कोऽपि वंशे नास्ति करोमि किम् ..
वह्निकुण्डात्समुत्थाय प्रोक्तवान्हव्यवाहनः .. 153 ..
17.17.m: There is no other suitable for her in [any] lineage. What shall I do?" / Rising from the fire-pit, the bearer of oblations spoke:

17.17.s:
śṛṇu me vacanaṃ vipra yo'syā bhartā bhaviṣyati ..
priyavratānvayabhavo mahābalaparākramaḥ .. 154 ..
17.17.d:
शृणु मे वचनं विप्र योऽस्या भर्ता भविष्यति ..
प्रियव्रतान्वयभवो महाबलपराक्रमः .. 154 ..
17.17.m: "Listen to my words, O brahmin, concerning who will be her husband: / Born in the lineage of Priyavrata, endowed with great strength and prowess,

17.17.s:
putro vikramaśīlasya kāliṃdījaṭharodbhavaḥ ..
durdamo nāma bhavitā bhartā hyasyā mahīpatiḥ .. 155 ..
17.17.d:
पुत्रो विक्रमशीलस्य कालिंदीजठरोद्भवः ..
दुर्दमो नाम भविता भर्ता ह्यस्या महीपतिः .. 155 ..
17.17.m: the son of Vikramaśīla, born from the womb of Kālindī, / the king named Durdama will indeed be her husband."

17.17.s:
atrāṃtare samāyāto durdamaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ ..
girau mṛgavadhākāṃkṣī muniṃ gehe na paśyati ..
priye'yi tātaḥ kva gata ehi satyaṃ bravīhi me .. 156 ..
17.17.d:
अत्रांतरे समायातो दुर्दमः स महीपतिः ..
गिरौ मृगवधाकांक्षी मुनिं गेहे न पश्यति ..
प्रियेऽयि तातः क्व गत एहि सत्यं ब्रवीहि मे .. 156 ..
17.17.m: In the meantime, that king Durdama arrived, / desiring to slay deer on the mountain. Not seeing the sage in the house, [he said:] / "Beloved, where has father gone? Come, tell me the truth!"

17.17.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
agniśālāsthitenaiva tacchrutaṃ vacanaṃ priyam ..
priyetyāmantraṇaṃ ko'yaṃ karoti mama veśmani .. .. 157 ..
17.17.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
अग्निशालास्थितेनैव तच्छ्रुतं वचनं प्रियम् ..
प्रियेत्यामन्त्रणं कोऽयं करोति मम वेश्मनि .. .. 157 ..
17.17.m: Nārada said: / Standing right in the sacrificial fire-chamber, he heard that dear speech: / "Who is this addressing [someone] as 'beloved' in my house?"

17.17.s:
sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ rājānaṃ durdamaṃ muniḥ ..
jaharṣa durdamaṃ dṛṣṭvā muniḥ prāha sa gautamam .. 158 ..
17.17.d:
स ददर्श महात्मानं राजानं दुर्दमं मुनिः ..
जहर्ष दुर्दमं दृष्ट्वा मुनिः प्राह स गौतमम् .. 158 ..
17.17.m: The sage saw the noble king Durdama. / Rejoicing upon seeing Durdama, the sage said to Gautama,

17.17.s:
śiṣyaṃ vinayasampannamarghyaṃ pādyaṃ samānaya ..
ekaṃ tāvadayaṃ bhūpaścirakālādupāgataḥ .. 159 ..
17.17.d:
शिष्यं विनयसम्पन्नमर्घ्यं पाद्यं समानय ..
एकं तावदयं भूपश्चिरकालादुपागतः .. 159 ..
17.17.m: his disciple endowed with humility: "Bring the arghya and pādya offerings! / For one thing, this king has arrived after a long time;

17.17.s:
jāmātā sāṃprataṃ rājā yogyāsya ca sutā mama ..
tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa rājā jāmātṛ kāraṇam.. 7.2.17.160 ..
17.17.d:
जामाता सांप्रतं राजा योग्यास्य च सुता मम ..
ततः स चिंतयामास राजा जामातृ कारणम्.. 7.2.17.160 ..
17.17.m: moreover, the king is now my son-in-law, and my daughter is suitable for him." / Then the king pondered the reason for [being called] a son-in-law.

17.17.s:
maunena vidhinā rājā jagṛhe'rghyaṃ dvijājñayā ..
tamāsanagataṃ vipro gṛhītārghyaṃ mahāmuniḥ .. 161 ..
17.17.d:
मौनेन विधिना राजा जगृहेऽर्घ्यं द्विजाज्ञया ..
तमासनगतं विप्रो गृहीतार्घ्यं महामुनिः .. 161 ..
17.17.m: In silence, according to the rule, the king received the arghya at the brahmin's command. / To him seated on a seat, who had accepted the arghya, the great sage, the brahmin,

17.17.s:
prastutaṃ prāha rājendraṃ nṛpate kuśalaṃ pure ..
kośe bale ca mitre ca bhṛtyāmātya prajāsu ca ..
tathātmani mahābāho yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam .. 162 ..
17.17.d:
प्रस्तुतं प्राह राजेन्द्रं नृपते कुशलं पुरे ..
कोशे बले च मित्रे च भृत्यामात्य प्रजासु च ..
तथात्मनि महाबाहो यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् .. 162 ..
17.17.m: spoke relevantly to the lord of kings: "O king, is all well in your city, / in your treasury, army, allies, servants, ministers, and subjects, / and likewise in yourself, O mighty-armed one, upon whom everything depends?

17.17.s:
patnī ca te kuśalinī yā'tra sthāne hi tiṣṭhati ..
anyāsāṃ kuśalaṃ brūhi yāḥ saṃti tava maṃdire .. 163 ..
17.17.d:
पत्नी च ते कुशलिनी याऽत्र स्थाने हि तिष्ठति ..
अन्यासां कुशलं ब्रूहि याः संति तव मंदिरे .. 163 ..
17.17.m: And is your wife well, who indeed stays here in this place? / Tell me also of the welfare of the other [wives] who are in your palace."

17.17.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
tvatprasādādakuśalaṃ nāsti rājye kvacinmama ..
jātakautūhalo'smyasmi mama bhāryā'tra kā mune .. 164 ..
17.17.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
त्वत्प्रसादादकुशलं नास्ति राज्ये क्वचिन्मम ..
जातकौतूहलोऽस्म्यस्मि मम भार्याऽत्र का मुने .. 164 ..
17.17.m: The king said: / "By your grace, there is no misfortune anywhere in my kingdom. / I have become curious about this: who is my wife here, O sage?"

17.17.s:
.. pramuca uvāca .. ..
revatī te varā bhāryā kiṃ na vetsi nṛpottama ..
trailokyasundarī yā tu kathaṃ sā vismṛtā tava .. 165 ..
17.17.d:
.. प्रमुच उवाच .. ..
रेवती ते वरा भार्या किं न वेत्सि नृपोत्तम ..
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी या तु कथं सा विस्मृता तव .. 165 ..
17.17.m: Pramuca said: / "Revatī is your excellent wife. Do you not know, O best of kings? / How have you forgotten her who is the beauty of the three worlds?"

17.17.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
subhadrāṃ śāṃtapāpāṃ ca kāverītanayāṃ tathā ..
sūrātmajānujātāṃ ca kadaṃbāṃ ca varaprajām .. 166 ..
17.17.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
सुभद्रां शांतपापां च कावेरीतनयां तथा ..
सूरात्मजानुजातां च कदंबां च वरप्रजाम् .. 166 ..
17.17.m: The king said: / "Subhadrā, Śāntapāpā, the daughter of Kāverī, / the younger sister of Sūrātmaja, Kadambā of excellent progeny,

17.17.s:
vipāṭhāṃ naṃdinīṃ caiva vedmi bhāryāṃ gṛhe mama ..
tiṣṭhanti naiva jānāmi bhāryā me revatī kutaḥ ...367 ..
ṛṣiruvāca .. ..
priyeti sāṃprataṃ proktā revatī sā priyā tava ..
tadanyathā na bhavitā vacanaṃ nṛpasattama .. 168 ..
.. rājovāca .. ..
nāsti bhāvakṛto doṣaḥ kṣamyatāṃ tadvaco mama ..
vinirgataṃ vacovaktrānnāhaṃ jāne dvijottama .. 169 ..
.. ṛṣiruvāca .. ..
nāsti bhāvakṛto doṣaḥ parivedmi kuruṣva tat ..
vahninā kathitastvaṃ me jāmātādya bhaviṣyasi .. 7.2.17.170 ..
ityādivacanai rājā bhāryā mene sa revatīm ..
ṛṣistathodyataḥ kartuṃ vivāhaṃ vidhi pūrvakam ..
uvāca kanyā pitaraṃ kiñcinme śrūyatāṃ pitaḥ .. 171 ..
yadi me patinā tāta vivāhaṃ kartumicchasi ..
revatyṛkṣaṃ vivāhaṃ me tatkarotu prasādataḥ .. 172 ..
17.17.d:
विपाठां नंदिनीं चैव वेद्मि भार्यां गृहे मम ..
तिष्ठन्ति नैव जानामि भार्या मे रेवती कुतः ...367 ..
ऋषिरुवाच .. ..
प्रियेति सांप्रतं प्रोक्ता रेवती सा प्रिया तव ..
तदन्यथा न भविता वचनं नृपसत्तम .. 168 ..
.. राजोवाच .. ..
नास्ति भावकृतो दोषः क्षम्यतां तद्वचो मम ..

The seer said: / "Just now you called her 'beloved'; that Revatī is your beloved. / That word cannot be otherwise, O best of kings!"
The king said: / "There was no fault of intention; may that utterance of mine be forgiven! / The word slipped from my mouth; I did not know [her], O best of brahmins!"
The seer said: / "There is no fault of intention; I know it completely, [yet] do it! / You were declared to me by the fire; today you shall become my son-in-law."
By these and other words, the king accepted Revatī as his wife. / When the seer was thus prepared to perform the marriage according to the rules, / the maiden said to her father: "Father, listen to something from me!
If you wish to perform my marriage with a husband, father, / let him perform my marriage under the Revatī constellation, out of grace."

The seer said: / "O gentle girl, the Revatī constellation does not stand in heaven in conjunction with the moon. / There are other constellations too, O fair-browed one, suitable for marriage."
The maiden said: / "Father, without that, time appears defective to me. / When time is defective, father, how can a marriage take place for one like me?"
Pramuca said: / "An ascetic renowned as Ṛtavāc felt anger toward Revatī; / being enraged, he cast down that constellation.
And she has been promised by me to him as his wife, as is known to you. / If you do not wish for the marriage, a crisis has come upon us!"
The maiden said: / "Did that sage Ṛtavāc alone perform austerity himself, / and not you, my father? Am I the daughter of a worthless brahmin?"
The seer said: / "You are not the daughter of a worthless brahmin; there is no ascetic superior to me. / You, my daughter, must be given away by me; I cannot undertake anything else."

17.17.m:
The maiden said: / "If my father is an ascetic, then why is this constellation not set up / again in the sky, and why is my marriage not performed then?"
The seer said:
"So be it! May good betide you, gentle girl; be pleased! / For your sake, I shall place the Revatī constellation back in the path of the moon."
Then, by the power of his austerity, the great sage, the best of brahmins, / restored the Revatī constellation just as before, in conjunction with the moon. / Having performed the marriage of his daughter, he spoke to his son-in-law:
"Tell me, O king, what wedding gift shall I give you? / Even if difficult to obtain, I shall grant it, for great austerity belongs to me."
The king said: / "I am born in the lineage of Manu Svāyambhuva, O sage. / By your grace, I choose a son who will be the lord of a manvantara."
The seer said: / "He will be a protector of the earth, endowed with great strength and prowess. / Revatī, having bathed in Revatīkuṇḍa, will give birth to a son."

Having done so, the king departed, and she gave birth to a son. / The name Raivata was given [to him]; he became the Manu, O king.
And by him it was declared then: 'On this Raivataka mountain, / women who take a ritual ablution will have sons of great strength, / long-lived, and free from grief and poverty.'
Nārada said: / When this was spoken, O king, that mountain became elongated and fell. / Those two deities, Hari and Śaṃkara, accompanied by their consorts, were remembered.
The moment they were remembered, they arrived then, because previously they were bound by him: / 'Wherever I am, there you two must dwell; this is certain.'
Therefore, the two deities Viṣṇu and Hara dwelt upon that best of mountains. / On the pleasant Raivataka mountain, by the water of the Svarṇarekhā river, / Revatī worshiped the deity Hari, and he said to her:
'May your union with the moon take place in the sky by the brahmin's command. / Choose another boon that is in your heart; I am pleased.'

Revatī said: / 'O God, you must always dwell upon the Raivataka mountain. / Wherever a ritual ablution was performed by me, the people who will bathe there—
may their abode be in the city of Viṣṇu: this is chosen by me.' / Having then said 'So be it,' four-armed Dāmodara dwelt upon the Raivataka mountain, / and Rudra himself also remained there.
All the rivers, headed by Gaṅgā, remained along with Viṣṇu. / But when the milk-ocean was being churned, when a tree arose
during the crushing of the gods and Daityas, therefore it was remembered as the āmalakī. / In this tree Lakṣmī is always present, O king, as in her father's house.
The tree is known as Śivā and Lakṣmī, and is served by the best among the gods. / By all the gods, headed by Brahmā, this tree is regarded as belonging to Viṣṇu.
Having deliberated, it was released formerly by all upon the Raivataka mountain. / Those who undertake a pilgrimage to this tree on the day of Hari,

on the eleventh lunar day in the bright fortnight of Phālguna, O best of kings, / their sons and grandsons will abound in virtues; / at the end, residence in the city of Viṣṇu comes to pass, there is no doubt here.
Bali said: / How is this Vaiṣṇava observance, dear to Viṣṇu, to be performed? / How is the night-vigil to be kept, by what rule? Tell that!
Nārada said: / Having fasted on the eleventh lunar day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, / having bathed in a river, pond, stepped well, ordinary well, or even at home,
and having gone to the mountain or into the forest, where that auspicious [tree] is found, / she is to be worshiped with lovely flowers, and men should keep a night-vigil.
A circumambulation of it is to be performed with one hundred and eight fruits. / Having circumambulated the tree, the fruit is to be eaten by men.
A water-pot filled with water must be provided together with a vessel; / food fit for oblations is to be prepared, and a lamp should be arranged according to rule.

17.17.m:
Thus the vigil is to be kept by those intent on listening to the sacred story. / Embodied beings are freed from the sins born of the Kali age and arising from the body.
At the end of their bodies, all those men are honored in the abode of Hari.
Sārasvata said: / Having spoken thus to the Daitya, Nārada went to the Raivataka mountain. / The king of the Daityas deliberated: 'What must be done by me now?'
'A conflict with the gods does not please me, O best of gods.'
The ministers said: / 'There is no great forbearance in the household of those noble kṣatriyas. / They will think [you] powerless, since they themselves advance. / Therefore, we ourselves shall advance together against the king of gods.'
Hearing this, he sounded the drum at first for the conflict with the gods. / Marshalling their army, the Daityas set out toward Mount Meru,
where that delightful city of the king of gods lies to the east. / Knowing that that army was advancing upon Mount Meru,

17.17.m:
by order of the king of gods, the army of the gods mobilized. / On the eastern side of Sumeru, a battle took place between the two.
When the entire army of the gods joined with the army of the Daityas, / a battle like the great dissolution then took place between the two.
Mounted upon Airāvaṇa, the king of gods arrived. / Mounted upon his chariot, the king of the Daityas and others arrived for battle.
Since the gods enjoy sacrificial offerings, they did not desire battle. / Airāvaṇa, seeing Bali, did not advance forward in the fight.
Surrounded by the directional elephants, he retreated in battle. / With the very arm by which Bali made the solemn vow at the sacrifice,
with that indeed he warded off all the gods in the encounter. / Being warded off, they turn back; what can the king of gods do?
The thunderbolt does not perform its work; released from the arm, it does not fly.
Thus many battles were terminated between the two then. / The Daityas of great strength could not be killed in battle by the gods.

17.17.m:
The gods remained, longing for strength; they were enlightened by their preceptor: / 'All the deities are immortal'—thus were they restrained by Śukra.
Knowing that Hari's fifth incarnation, Vāmana, was present, / the lord of the gods, overjoyed, ruled in Amarāvatī.
The king of the Daityas danced in battle; in his own house he worshiped the gods. / Daityas departed to Pātāla, while mortals ruled.
Then all the hosts of gods took counsel together with the deities: / 'The Daitya rules two worlds, and the lord of the gods rules heaven.
He should be tolerated only so long as Vāmana goes to the Raivata mountain; / silence must be maintained by the gods, even though conquered by the Daityas.'
Ever since Vāmana was born upon the surface of the earth, / ever since then, bad omens arose for the Daityas.
A female jackal enters the city and howls discordantly at night. / Crows wander screeching in the city by day and by night.

Serpents slither into the houses—black, dreadful, and full of fierce poison. / Herons, vultures, and cranes circle bewildered over the city.
Defective fetuses are born to women, cows, or female deer. / There is neither ghee nor milk, and no oil is found in sesame.
Country-folk fight continually among the people, / and [there appears] Kālī, with terrible face, long hair, and [wide-open] eyes.
Unrecognized, weeping, she goes from house to house in the city. / "Who is this? From where?" An ascetic smeared with ash is not known.
An ascetic vowed to silence walks naked ahead to every house, / and behind he plays the damaru and makes the "huṃ" roar.
Unseasonably, enraged clouds release abundant water; / the pits are filled with hailstones, and the mountains rumble greatly.
An earthquake occurred, and the burning of the quarters also occurred. / The whole pack of dogs, gathering together and raising their muzzles high,

howls constantly in the city at night; the owl hoots its call. / The destruction of Bali's kingdom has come; a comet rises in the sky at night.
A pierce made by stakes is seen upon the sun's orb; / the moon does not shine in the sky crowded with headless trunks.
That piercing of Rohiṇī occurred which occurs at the end of a yuga; / by day, stars are counted by the people with the sharpest faculties.
Inversion occurred among the seeds, and in the earth, women, cows, and deer; / horses suddenly neigh, and elephants display no rut.
The counsel deliberated by the ministers is foiled at the destruction of the kingdom; / the fire consecrated with offerings of ghee does not blaze then for the twice-born.
A violent wind blows, trees are swirled about by a whirlwind; / banners burn on shrines, and the sky becomes dusky grey.
These and many other portents occurred in the house of the mighty [Bali], / once Vāmana was born, following the arrival of Nārada.

17.17.m:
Moreover, another terrible thing occurs: the seeing of dreams by day. / When the Daityas put on their armor, having fallen, they fall down again.
Seeing such omens concerning his army, he does not march forth; / Bali constantly remains in his house and rules the kingdom.
There is no comfort in his body: bodily fatigue and headache [afflict him]; / feverish, he does not sleep well, he does not eat, nor does he drink; / food eaten is not digested; the whole populace too is thrown into distress.
Seeing the world topsy-turvy, Bali, his mind troubled, / deliberated, grieved, along with the brahmins: "What is this?"
Summoning the guru Śukra and seating him in the assembly, / the Daitya, filled with supreme devotion, asked him about welfare: / "All this is turning upside-down; tell me that [cause].
O guru, what was spoken to me by Nārada will surely come true; / tell me, together with the brahmins, what pacifies these portents."

17.17.m:
Śukra said: / "For the pacification of portents, a sacrifice with one's entire wealth as sacrificial fee should be performed; / let a twelve-year [sacrifice] be undertaken together with the brahmins and kṣatriyas.
Let whatever ṛṣis, brahmins, munis, and celibate students there are, / even those residing far away, come to the great sacrifice.
To the east of the city, a sacrificial pavilion should be built. / Whatever gift is pleasing to each and every one must be given by you, O king." / Saying "I shall do so," he applied himself to the sacrifice.
Summoning all the brahmins skilled in sacrificial rites, / the sacrificial initiation was undertaken by them in the sacrifice of all one's wealth.
"My whole wealth is to be given by me to a brahmin here upon request; / if asked, I shall give my body, sons, friends, and wives.
A gift must constantly be given by me to the brahmins in this sacrifice; / even if forbidden, I shall not desist; I must surely give. / If I do not give when asked, then my sacrifice will be in vain."

17.17.m:
Having constructed a divine pavilion many yojanas wide, / gifts are given there, as well as food and clothing.
The seven ṛṣis came down to the surface of the earth from the sky; / all the brahmins who exist on earth arrived from all quarters.
And kṣatriyas arrived bringing diverse wealth; / they offer it to the king as the sacrificial rite commences.
From as far as the ocean came actors, dancers, and supplicants; / the roar of singing and musical instruments blended with the sound of the Vedas.
The cry "Give! Give!" being petitioned deafened the three worlds; / there is no word "Do not give!", nor is there "Give a little!"
Whatever thing whoever asks for, that is given to him there. / Indeed, there is not even a brahmin who asks him for much [more than needed].
And the twice-born do not accept [only] for food and clothing / gold, jewels, silver, or horses, chariots, and elephants.
Houses, cattle, land, and villages the twice-born do not take; / satisfied with Bali's rule, what would they do with wealth?

17.17.m:
Thus proceeds the great sacrifice with all one's wealth as sacrificial fee.
Others dance, sing, and recite, praising the sacrifice accompanied by lavish gifts; / Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, the planets, the sun, and the moon are propitiated with oblations and mantras.
Some praise Bali, others the guru, some the Hotṛ priest, and some the retinue: / "[This sacrifice is like that] neither of Prajāpati nor of the lord of the gods; and when it concludes, he will certainly go / to Rasātala, together with his sons and friends, having bestowed the kingdom upon the best of the twice-born."
Such words the brahmins utter; the Daityas hear them: "What is this they say?" / Meeting together, those standing before Bali tell him; Bali, overjoyed, gives what is asked.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "Description of the Power of Bali's Sacrifice," in the Second [Book], the Vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmya, in the Seventh [Section], the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
